commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
श्री गणेशायः नमः
गुरुं नत्वा शिवं साक्षात् ब्रह्मानन्देन तन्यते ।
इदानीन्तनानां सुबोधार्थमस्याः सुविज्ञायगोरक्षसिद्धान्तहार्दम् ।
मुमुक्षुजनहितार्थं राजयोगद्वारा कैवल्यप्रदां हठप्रदीपिकां विधित्सुः परमकारुणिकः स्वात्मरामयोगीन्द्रः तत्प्रत्यूहनिवृत्तये हठयोगप्रवर्तकश्रीमदादिनाथनमस्कारलक्षणं मङ्गलं तावदाचरति -श्रीआधिनाथेत्यादिना । तस्मै श्रीआदिनाथाय नमोऽस्त्विति अन्वयः । आदिश्चासौ नाथश्च आदिनाथः सर्वेश्वरः । श्रीशब्दः आदिः यस्य सः श्रीआदिः, श्रीआदिश्चासौ नाथश्च श्रीआदिनाथः, तस्मै श्रीआदिनाथाय । श्रीनाथाय विष्णवे वा इत्यर्थः । श्रीआदिनाथाय इत्यत्र यणभावस्तु ‘अपि माषं मषं कुर्यात् छन्दोभङ्गं त्यजेद्गिराम्’ इति छन्दोविदां संप्रदायादुच्चारणसौष्ठवाच्चेति बोध्यम् । वस्तुतस्तु असंहितपाठस्वीकारापेक्षया श्रीआदिनाथायेति पाठस्वीकारेऽप्रवृत्तनित्यविध्युद्देश्यतावच्छेदकानाक्रान्तत्वेन परिनिष्ठितत्वसंभवात् सम्प्रत्युदाहृतदृष्टान्तद्वयस्यापीदृग्विषयवैषम्यात्, नित्यसाहित्यभङ्गजनितदोषस्य शाब्दिकाननुमतत्वाच्चासंमृष्टविधेयांशतारूपदोषस्य साहित्यकारैरुक्तत्वेऽपि क्वचित् तैरप्यस्वीकृतत्वेन शाब्दिकाचार्यैरेकाजित्यादौ कर्मधारयस्वीकरणेन सर्वथानादृतत्वाच्च लाघावतिशय इति सुधियो विभावयन्तु । नमः प्रह्वीभावोऽस्तु । प्रार्थनायां लोट् । तस्मै, कस्मै इत्यपेक्षायामाह - येनेति । येन आदिनाथेन उपदिष्टा गिरिजायै हठयोगविद्या हश्च ठश्च हठौ सूर्यचन्द्रौ तयोर्योगो हठयोगः, एतेन हठशब्दवाच्ययोः सूर्यचन्द्राख्ययोः प्राणापानयोरैक्यलक्षणः प्राणायामो हठयोग इति हठयोगस्य लक्षणं सिद्धम् । तथा चोक्तं गोरक्षनाथेन सिद्धसिद्धान्तपद्धतौ -
हकारः कीर्तितः सूर्यष्ठकारश्चन्द्र उच्यते ।
तत्प्रतिपादिका विद्या हठयोगविद्या, हठयोगशास्त्रमिति यावत् । गिरिजायै आदिनाथकृतो हठविद्योपदेशो महकालयोगशास्त्रादौ प्रसिद्धः । प्रकर्षेण उन्नतः प्रोन्नतः । मन्त्रयोगहठयोगादीनाम् अधरभूमीनामुत्तरभूमित्वात् राजयोगस्य प्रोन्नतत्वम् । राजयोगश्च सर्ववृत्तिनिरोधलक्षणोऽसंप्रज्ञातयोगः । तम् इच्छोर्मुमुक्षोः अधिरोहिणीव, अधिरुह्यते अन्या इत्यधिरोहिणी निःश्रेणीव विभ्राजते विशेषेण भ्राजते शोभते । यथा प्रोन्नतसौधमारोढुम् इच्छोः अधिरोहिणी अनायासेन सौधप्रापिका भवति एवं हठदीपिकापि प्रोन्नतराजयोगम् आरोढुमुच्छोः अनायसेन राजयोगप्रापिका भवतीति । उपमालङ्कारः । इन्द्रवज्राख्यं वृत्तम् ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Salutations to Shri Ganesha. Having bowed to the Guru and Lord Shiva directly, this (commentary) is expanded by Brahmānanda. For the easy understanding of the people of this current age, having thoroughly understood the essence of Gorakṣa's Siddhānta (philosophy). The most compassionate Yogīndra Svātmārāma, wishing to compose the Haṭha Pradīpikā, which grants liberation (Kaivalya) through Rāja Yoga for the benefit of those desiring liberation, now performs the auspicious act (maṅgala) of saluting Shri Ādinātha, the promulgator of Haṭhayoga, for the removal of obstacles. (This is indicated by the phrase) 'Śrī-Ādināthāya, etc.' The grammatical connection (anvaya) is 'Salutation be to that glorious Ādinātha.' Ādinātha means 'the first Lord,' the universal Lord. Alternatively, 'Śrī-ādi' means 'one whose beginning is Śrī (glory/Lakshmi),' and 'Śrī-ādinātha' means 'that Lord whose beginning is Śrī,' to that glorious Primordial Lord. It can also mean 'to Śrīnātha, i.e., Viṣṇu.' The non-application of 'yaṇa' Sandhi in 'Śrīādināthāya' is to be understood from the tradition of prosodists who state, 'one may turn a black gram into a pea, but one should avoid breaking the meter of verses,' and for the ease of pronunciation. In fact, compared to accepting a non-Sandhi reading, accepting 'Śrīādināthāya' as is, prevents it from being subject to the conditions of an unactivated eternal rule, thus allowing it to be a complete form. Furthermore, the two examples cited now also demonstrate this subject's complexity. Moreover, the defect arising from breaking the eternal literary cohesion is not approved by grammarians. Although the flaw of 'asaṁmṛṣṭa-vidheyāṁśatā' (having an unclear predicate part) is mentioned by literary critics, it is sometimes not accepted even by them, and grammarian preceptors, by accepting 'karmadhāraya' in cases like 'ekāj,' have completely disregarded it, thus resulting in great conciseness. Let the wise consider this. 'Namaḥ' means 'let there be bowing/prostration.' The imperative mood (loṭ) is used for prayer. In anticipation of the question 'to whom?' regarding 'tasmai' (to Him), the verse says 'yena' (by whom). By that Ādinātha, the science of Haṭhayoga was taught to Girijā (Pārvatī). 'Ha' (ह) and 'Ṭha' (ठ) refer to the sun and moon respectively. The union (yoga) of these two (sun and moon) is Haṭhayoga. By this, the definition of Haṭhayoga as the unification (aikya) of Prāṇa and Apāna, which are referred to by the words 'Ha' (sun) and 'Ṭha' (moon), is established as Prāṇāyāma. And it has been stated by Gorakṣanātha in the Siddha Siddhānta Paddhati: 'The letter 'Ha' is known as the sun, and the letter 'Ṭha' is said to be the moon.' The knowledge that expounds this (union) is Haṭhayogavidyā, or in other words, the scripture of Haṭhayoga. The instruction of Haṭha Vidya by Ādinātha to Girijā is famous in texts like Mahākāla Yoga Śāstra. 'Pronnata' means 'eminently elevated.' Rāja Yoga is eminently elevated because it is the higher stage (uttarabhūmi) compared to the lower stages (adharabhūmi) of Mantra Yoga, Haṭha Yoga, etc. Rāja Yoga is characterized by the cessation of all mental modifications (sarva-vṛtti-nirodha), which is known as Asamprajñāta Yoga. For one who desires that (Rāja Yoga), for the seeker of liberation (mumukṣu), it (Haṭha Pradīpikā) shines forth like a ladder (adhirohiṇī), a staircase by which one ascends. Just as a ladder easily helps one reach a high palace (saudha), so too the Haṭha Pradīpikā easily helps one desirous of ascending to the elevated Rāja Yoga attain Rāja Yoga. This is an Upamālaṅkāra (simile). The meter is named Indravajrā.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: श्री गणेश को नमस्कार। गुरु और साक्षात् शिव को प्रणाम करके, ब्रह्मानन्द द्वारा यह (व्याख्या) विस्तारित की जा रही है। वर्तमान युग के लोगों को सुगमता से समझाने के लिए, गोरक्ष सिद्धांत के गूढ़ रहस्य को भली-भांति जानकर। मोक्ष की इच्छा रखने वाले लोगों के हित के लिए, राजयोग के माध्यम से कैवल्य प्रदान करने वाली हठप्रदीपिका की रचना करने के इच्छुक अत्यंत करुणामय योगीन्द्र स्वात्मराम, बाधाओं को दूर करने के लिए, हठयोग के प्रवर्तक श्री आदिनाथ को नमस्कार करने रूपी मंगल कार्य का आचरण करते हैं - "श्री आदिनाथाय" इत्यादि से। "तस्मै श्री आदिनाथाय नमोऽस्तु" यह अन्वय है। 'आदिनाथ' का अर्थ है 'प्रथम नाथ' या 'सर्वेश्वर'। 'श्री आदि' का अर्थ है 'जिसका आदि श्री है', और 'श्री आदिनाथ' का अर्थ है 'वह नाथ जिसका आदि श्री है', ऐसे श्री आदिनाथ को (नमस्कार)। अथवा 'श्रीनाथ' अर्थात भगवान विष्णु को (नमस्कार)। "श्रीआदिनाथाय" यहाँ यण् संधि के अभाव को "अपि माषं मषं कुर्यात् छन्दोभङ्गं त्यजेद्गिराम्" (छंद भंग न हो, तो माष को मष भी कर दे) इस छंदोविदों के संप्रदाय और उच्चारण की सुगमता के कारण समझना चाहिए। वस्तुतः, असंहित पाठ स्वीकार करने की अपेक्षा "श्रीआदिनाथाय" इस पाठ को स्वीकार करने में अप्रवृत्त नित्यविधि के उद्देश्यतावच्छेदकों से अनाक्रान्त होने के कारण इसकी परिनिष्ठितता संभव है, और अब तक उद्धृत दोनों दृष्टांतों में भी ऐसे विषयगत वैषम्य के कारण, नित्य साहित्य भंग से उत्पन्न दोष को वैयाकरणों द्वारा अस्वीकृत होने के कारण, और 'असंमृष्टविधेयांशता' नामक दोष को साहित्यकारों द्वारा कहा गया होने पर भी कहीं-कहीं उनके द्वारा भी अस्वीकृत होने तथा वैयाकरण आचार्यों द्वारा 'एकाजि' इत्यादि में कर्मधारय को स्वीकार कर उसे सर्वथा अनादृत करने के कारण अत्यधिक लाघव है, ऐसा बुद्धिमानों को विचार करना चाहिए। 'नमः' का अर्थ 'प्रह्वीभाव' (नमन) हो। लोट् लकार प्रार्थना में है। 'तस्मै' (उसको) - किसको? इस अपेक्षा पर कहते हैं - 'येन' (जिसके द्वारा)। जिस आदिनाथ द्वारा गिरिजायै (पार्वती को) हठयोगविद्या का उपदेश दिया गया। 'ह' और 'ठ' सूर्य और चंद्रमा हैं, उन दोनों का योग 'हठयोग' है। इससे 'हठ' शब्द द्वारा कहे गए सूर्य और चंद्रमा नामक प्राण और अपान के एकीकरण (ऐक्य) रूप प्राणायाम को हठयोग कहा गया है, इस प्रकार हठयोग का लक्षण सिद्ध होता है। जैसा कि गोरक्षनाथ ने सिद्धसिद्धान्तपद्धति में कहा है - 'हकार' सूर्य कहा गया है और 'ठकार' चंद्रमा कहा जाता है। उसका प्रतिपादन करने वाली विद्या हठयोगविद्या है, अर्थात हठयोगशास्त्र। आदिनाथ द्वारा गिरिजायै (पार्वती को) हठविद्या का उपदेश महकालयोगशास्त्र आदि में प्रसिद्ध है। 'प्रकर्षेण उन्नतः' अर्थात् 'प्रोन्नतः' (अत्यंत उन्नत)। राजयोग, मंत्रयोग, हठयोग आदि अधर भूमियों (निचले स्तरों) की उत्तरभूमि (ऊँचा स्तर) होने के कारण प्रोन्नत (अत्यंत उन्नत) है। राजयोग सभी चित्तवृत्तियों के निरोध (रोकने) के लक्षण वाला असंप्रज्ञात योग है। उसको चाहने वाले मुमुक्षु (मोक्षार्थी) के लिए यह (हठप्रदीपिका) एक अधिरोहिणी (सीढ़ी) के समान, जिस पर चढ़कर ऊपर जाया जाता है, निःश्रेणी (सीढ़ी) के समान विशेष रूप से सुशोभित होती है। जैसे एक ऊँचे महल पर चढ़ने की इच्छा रखने वाले के लिए सीढ़ी बिना प्रयास के महल तक पहुँचा देती है, वैसे ही हठदीपिका भी उन्नत राजयोग पर चढ़ने की इच्छा रखने वाले के लिए बिना प्रयास के राजयोग की प्राप्ति कराती है। यह उपमा अलंकार है। इसका वृत्त इंद्रवज्रा नामक है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Guru Parampara (Lineage of Teachers) and the origin of Haṭhayoga
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse serves as a maṅgalācaraṇam (auspicious invocation), offering salutations to Ādinātha (Lord Shiva), who is revered as the original promulgator of Haṭhayoga. It reflects the traditional Indian practice of commencing a treatise with an invocation to a deity or guru, acknowledging the divine source of knowledge and seeking blessings for the successful completion of the work.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse underscores the deep respect for knowledge, its transmission through a spiritual lineage (Guru-paramparā), and the importance of acknowledging the source of wisdom in Indian culture. In a practical sense, it emphasizes humility, gratitude, and the recognition that profound wisdom often originates from ancient, revered traditions and figures, which remains highly relevant in modern learning and personal development.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The primary practice prescribed is Namaskāra (salutation) as an act of maṅgala (auspicious beginning) to remove obstacles (pratyyūha-nivṛtti). More broadly, the text introduces Haṭhayoga as Prāṇāyāma (breath control), which involves uniting Prāṇa and Apāna, intended as a preparatory step (adharabhūmi) for Rāja Yoga (meditative absorption) which is the ultimate Kaivalya-pradā (liberation-granting) practice.
commentary_faqs.answer: The core concept is Maṅgalācaraṇam, an auspicious invocation, specifically a Namaskāra (salutation) to Śrīādinātha (Lord Shiva, the primordial Guru of Yoga). The bhashya extensively unpacks the etymology of Haṭhayoga as the union of Ha (sun/Prāṇa) and Ṭha (moon/Apāna), emphasizing it as Prāṇāyāma leading to Rāja Yoga. Rāja Yoga is defined as Sarva-vṛtti-nirodha (cessation of all mental modifications) or Asamprajñāta Yoga, highlighting the hierarchical progression of yogic practices towards Kaivalya (liberation).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: From a secular and psychological perspective, the 'Maṅgalācaraṇam' reflects the psychological benefit of setting positive intentions and acknowledging sources of inspiration before embarking on a significant endeavor. The emphasis on Haṭhayoga as Prāṇāyāma (breath control) resonates with modern understanding of mindfulness and stress reduction, where regulated breathing is a key tool for emotional regulation and cognitive clarity. The idea of a progressive path from physical practices to higher states of mental control (Rāja Yoga as cessation of mental modifications) aligns with modern therapeutic approaches that integrate body-mind practices to achieve mental well-being, focus, and inner peace. The metaphor of Haṭhayoga as a 'ladder' to Rāja Yoga suggests a structured, step-by-step approach to self-mastery, a valuable model for any personal or professional development goal.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: एवं परमगुरुनमस्कारलक्षणं मङ्गलं कृत्वा विघ्नबाहुल्ये मङ्गलबाहुल्यस्याप्यपेक्षितत्वात् स्वगुरुनमस्कारात्मकं मङ्गलमाचरन्नस्य ग्रन्थस्य विषयप्रयोजनादीन् प्रदर्शयति - प्रणम्येति । श्रीमन्तं गुरुं श्रीगुरुं नाथं श्रीगुरुनाथं, स्वगुरुमिति यावत् । प्रणम्य प्रकर्षेणभक्तिपूर्वकं नत्वा स्वामारामेण योगिना योगोऽस्यास्तीति तेन । केवलं राजयोगाय केवलं राजयोगार्थं हठविद्योपदिश्यते इत्यन्वयः । हठविद्याया राजयोग एव मुख्यं फलं न सिद्धय इति केवलपदस्याभिप्रायः । सिद्धयस्त्वानुषङ्गिक्यः । एतेन राजयोगफलसहितो हठयोगोऽस्य ग्रन्थस्य विषयः । राजयोगद्वारा कैवल्यं चास्य फलम् । तत्कामश्चाधिकारी । ग्रन्थविषययोः प्रतिपाद्यप्रतिपादकभावस्संबन्धः । ग्रन्थस्य कैवल्यस्य च प्रयोज्यप्रयोजकभावः संबन्धः । ग्रन्थाभिधेयस्य सफलयोगस्य कैवल्यस्य च साध्यसाधनभावः संबन्धः इत्युक्तम् ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Thus, having performed an auspicious invocation (maṅgala) characterized by bowing to the Supreme Guru (paramaguru), and since in the abundance of obstacles, an abundance of auspicious invocations is also desired, the author, performing an auspicious invocation in the form of bowing to his own Guru (svaguru), thereupon reveals the subject matter, purpose, and other aspects of this text, by saying 'Praṇamya' (having bowed). 'Śrīmantaṃ guruṃ' means 'Śrīguruṃ', and 'nāthaṃ' means 'Śrīgurunāthaṃ', that is to say, one's own Guru. 'Praṇamya' means having bowed with profound devotion. 'Svātmārāmeṇa yoginā' means by the Yogi who possesses Yoga, i.e., Svātmārāma. The syntactic connection (anvaya) is: 'Haṭhavidyā is taught solely for Rāja Yoga, solely for the purpose of Rāja Yoga.' The import of the word 'kevalam' (solely) is that Rāja Yoga alone is the main fruit of Haṭha Vidyā, not the *siddhis* (yogic powers). The *siddhis*, however, are incidental. By this, Haṭha Yoga, accompanied by the fruit of Rāja Yoga, is the subject matter of this text. And Kaivalya (absolute liberation) through Rāja Yoga is its ultimate fruit. One who desires that (Kaivalya) is the qualified aspirant (adhikārin). The relationship between the text and its subject matter is that of the explainer and the explained. The relationship between the text and Kaivalya is that of the means and the end achieved. The relationship between the successful Yoga (as expounded in the text) and Kaivalya is that of the means and the end (sādhya-sādhana bhāva). Thus, it has been stated.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: इस प्रकार, परमगुरु को नमस्कार रूपी मंगल करके (पूर्व श्लोक में), और चूंकि विघ्नों की अधिकता होने पर अधिक मंगल की भी अपेक्षा होती है, इसलिए अब अपने गुरु को नमस्कार रूपी मंगल करते हुए, लेखक इस ग्रंथ के विषय, प्रयोजन आदि को 'प्रणम्य' पद से प्रदर्शित करते हैं। 'श्रीमन्तं गुरुं' का अर्थ 'श्रीगुरुं' है, और 'नाथं' का अर्थ 'श्रीगुरुनाथं' है, अर्थात् अपने गुरु को। 'प्रणम्य' का अर्थ है विशेष भक्तिपूर्वक नमस्कार करके। 'स्वात्मारामेण योगिना' का अर्थ है उस योगी के द्वारा जिसमें योग है, अर्थात् स्वात्माराम के द्वारा। अन्वय यह है कि 'केवल राजयोग के लिए ही हठविद्या का उपदेश किया जाता है'। 'केवलं' पद का अभिप्राय यह है कि हठविद्या का मुख्य फल केवल राजयोग ही है, सिद्धियाँ नहीं। सिद्धियाँ तो आनुषंगिक होती हैं। इससे यह स्पष्ट होता है कि राजयोग के फल सहित हठयोग इस ग्रंथ का विषय है। और राजयोग के माध्यम से कैवल्य (मोक्ष) इसका परम फल है। उस कैवल्य की इच्छा रखने वाला ही अधिकारी है। ग्रंथ और विषय के बीच प्रतिपाद्य-प्रतिपादक भाव (जो समझाया जाए और जो समझाए) का संबंध है। ग्रंथ और कैवल्य के बीच प्रयोज्य-प्रयोजक भाव (जो प्राप्त किया जाए और जो प्राप्त करने का साधन हो) का संबंध है। ग्रंथ में वर्णित सफल योग और कैवल्य के बीच साध्य-साधन भाव (लक्ष्य और उसे प्राप्त करने का साधन) का संबंध है – ऐसा कहा गया है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Reverence for the Guru and the purpose of the yogic text.
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse functions as a traditional *maṅgala-ācaraṇa* (auspicious invocation) at the commencement of a spiritual text. It highlights the profound importance of offering obeisance to one's spiritual preceptor (Guru) as an act of humility and gratitude, essential for successful spiritual endeavor. The author, Svātmārāma, identifies himself, indicating his internal orientation towards Self-realization as the foundation for the teachings to follow.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: The tradition of Guru-praṇāma (bowing to the Guru) is a cornerstone of Indian spiritual and educational systems, signifying respect for the lineage of knowledge and the mentor's guidance. In contemporary life, it emphasizes the value of mentorship, acknowledging the contributions of teachers and guides, and fostering a receptive attitude crucial for deep learning and personal development in any field, promoting a culture of humility and continuous learning.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The primary practice prescribed is bowing to the Guru (*Guru-praṇāma*) with profound devotion (*prakarṣeṇabhaktipūrvakaṃ natvā*). More broadly, the text implies diligent practice of *Haṭha Vidyā* as a preparatory step for *Rāja Yoga*. The practice is explicitly goal-oriented, with the ultimate aim being *Kaivalya*, rather than lesser attainments like *siddhis*, which are deemed secondary.
commentary_faqs.answer: The core concept established is the *anubandha-catuṣṭaya* (fourfold connection) for the *Hatha Yoga Pradipika*. The commentary clarifies that *Haṭha Yoga* is a *sādhana* (means) leading *kevalam* (solely) to *Rāja Yoga*, which is the direct path to *Kaivalya* (ultimate liberation, the aloneness of the Puruṣa). It explicitly states that *siddhis* (yogic powers) are merely *ānuṣaṅgikī* (incidental) and not the *mukhya phalam* (primary fruit). The initial *svaguru-namaskāra* serves as a *maṅgala-ācaraṇa* (auspicious invocation) for successful completion of the text.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In a modern secular and psychological context, the verse and commentary highlight the importance of reverence for mentors and teachers, fostering a mindset of humility and receptivity essential for deep learning and personal growth. The distinction between the ultimate goal (*Rāja Yoga* / *Kaivalya*) and incidental benefits (*siddhis*) is highly relevant; it encourages individuals to pursue mastery, inner peace, or self-actualization over superficial achievements or external validations. Psychologically, this approach helps maintain focus, preventing distraction by transient successes and reinforcing the value of a clear, sustained purpose in any self-development or skill-building endeavor.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
ननु मन्त्रयोगसगुणध्याननिर्गुणध्यानमुद्रादिभिरेव राजयोगसिद्धौ किं हठविद्योपदेशेनेत्याशङ्क्य व्युत्थितचित्तानां मन्त्रयोगादिभिः राजयोगसिद्धेः, हठयोगादेव राजयोगसिद्धिं वदन् ग्रन्थं प्रतिजानीते -
ज्ञानभूमिः शुभेच्छाख्या प्रथमा समुदाहृता ।
सत्त्वापत्तिश्चतुर्थी स्यात् ततोऽसंसक्तिनामिका ॥
परार्थाभाविनी षष्ठी सप्तमी तुर्यगा स्मृता ॥
अस्यार्थः - शुभेच्छा इत्याख्या यस्याः सा शुभेच्छाख्या । विवेकवैराग्ययुता शमादिपूर्विका तीव्रमुमुक्षा प्रथमा ज्ञानस्य भूमिः । भूमिका उदाहृता कथिता । योगिभिरिति शेषः । १ । विचारणा श्रवणमननात्मिका द्वितीया ज्ञानभूमिः स्यात् । २ । अनेकार्थग्राहकं मनो यदानेकार्थान् परित्यज्य सदेकार्थवृत्तिप्रवाहवद्भवति तदा तनु मानसं यस्यां सा तनुमानसा निदिध्यासनरूपा तृतीया ज्ञानभूमिः स्यादिति शेषः । ३ । इमास्तिस्रः साधनभूमिकाः । आसु भूमिषु साधक इत्युच्यते । तिसृभिर्भूमिकाभिः शुद्धसत्त्वेऽन्तः करणेऽहं ब्रह्मास्मीत्याकारिकापरोक्षवृत्तिरूपा सत्त्वापत्तिनामिका चतुर्थी ज्ञानभूमिः स्यात् । चतुर्थीयं फलभूमिः । अस्यां योगी ब्रह्मविदित्युच्यते । इयं संप्रज्ञातयोगभूमिका । ४ । वक्षमाणास्तिस्रोऽसंप्रज्ञातयोगभूमयः । सत्त्वापत्तेरनन्तरा सत्त्वापत्तिसंज्ञिकायां भूमावुपस्थितासु सिद्धिषु असंसक्तस्यासंसक्तिनामिका पञ्चमी ज्ञानभूमिः स्यात् ।
अस्यां योगी स्वयमेव व्युत्थिष्ठते । एतां भूमिं प्राप्तो ब्रह्मविद्वर इत्युच्यते । ५ ।
परब्रह्मातिरिक्तमर्थं न भावयति यस्यां सा परार्थाभाविनी षष्ठी ज्ञानभूमिः स्यात् । अस्यां योगी परप्रबोधित एव व्युत्थितो भवति । एतां प्राप्तो ब्रह्मविद्वरीयानित्युच्यते । ६ । तुर्यगा नाम सप्तमी भूमिः स्मृता । अस्यां योगी स्वतः परतो वा न व्युत्थानं प्राप्नोति । एतां प्राप्तो ब्रह्मविद्वरिष्ठ इत्युच्यते । ७ । तत्र प्रमाणभूता श्रुतिरत्रैवोक्ता पूर्वम् । अयमेव जीवन्मुक्त इत्युच्यते, स एव स्वात्मरामपदेनोक्त इत्यलं बहूक्तेन ॥ ३ ॥
commentaries.text:
ननु मन्त्रयोगसगुणध्याननिर्गुणध्यानमुद्रादिभिरेव राजयोगसिद्धौ किं हठविद्योपदेशेनेत्याशङ्क्य व्युत्थितचित्तानां मन्त्रयोगादिभिः राजयोगसिद्धेः, हठयोगादेव राजयोगसिद्धिं वदन् ग्रन्थं प्रतिजानीते -
ज्ञानभूमिः शुभेच्छाख्या प्रथमा समुदाहृता ।
सत्त्वापत्तिश्चतुर्थी स्यात् ततोऽसंसक्तिनामिका ॥
परार्थाभाविनी षष्ठी सप्तमी तुर्यगा स्मृता ॥
अस्यार्थः - शुभेच्छा इत्याख्या यस्याः सा शुभेच्छाख्या । विवेकवैराग्ययुता शमादिपूर्विका तीव्रमुमुक्षा प्रथमा ज्ञानस्य भूमिः । भूमिका उदाहृता कथिता । योगिभिरिति शेषः । १ । विचारणा श्रवणमननात्मिका द्वितीया ज्ञानभूमिः स्यात् । २ । अनेकार्थग्राहकं मनो यदानेकार्थान् परित्यज्य सदेकार्थवृत्तिप्रवाहवद्भवति तदा तनु मानसं यस्यां सा तनुमानसा निदिध्यासनरूपा तृतीया ज्ञानभूमिः स्यादिति शेषः । ३ । इमास्तिस्रः साधनभूमिकाः । आसु भूमिषु साधक इत्युच्यते । तिसृभिर्भूमिकाभिः शुद्धसत्त्वेऽन्तः करणेऽहं ब्रह्मास्मीत्याकारिकापरोक्षवृत्तिरूपा सत्त्वापत्तिनामिका चतुर्थी ज्ञानभूमिः स्यात् । चतुर्थीयं फलभूमिः । अस्यां योगी ब्रह्मविदित्युच्यते । इयं संप्रज्ञातयोगभूमिका । ४ । वक्षमाणास्तिस्रोऽसंप्रज्ञातयोगभूमयः । सत्त्वापत्तेरनन्तरा सत्त्वापत्तिसंज्ञिकायां भूमावुपस्थितासु सिद्धिषु असंसक्तस्यासंसक्तिनामिका पञ्चमी ज्ञानभूमिः स्यात् ।
अस्यां योगी स्वयमेव व्युत्थिष्ठते । एतां भूमिं प्राप्तो ब्रह्मविद्वर इत्युच्यते । ५ ।
परब्रह्मातिरिक्तमर्थं न भावयति यस्यां सा परार्थाभाविनी षष्ठी ज्ञानभूमिः स्यात् । अस्यां योगी परप्रबोधित एव व्युत्थितो भवति । एतां प्राप्तो ब्रह्मविद्वरीयानित्युच्यते । ६ । तुर्यगा नाम सप्तमी भूमिः स्मृता । अस्यां योगी स्वतः परतो वा न व्युत्थानं प्राप्नोति । एतां प्राप्तो ब्रह्मविद्वरिष्ठ इत्युच्यते । ७ । तत्र प्रमाणभूता श्रुतिरत्रैवोक्ता पूर्वम् । अयमेव जीवन्मुक्त इत्युच्यते, स एव स्वात्मरामपदेनोक्त इत्यलं बहूक्तेन ॥ ३ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Objection: Since Rajayoga can be achieved through Mantrayoga, Saguna-dhyana, Nirguna-dhyana, Mudras, etc., what is the use of teaching Hathavidya? Anticipating this doubt, the author begins the text by stating that for those whose minds are distracted, Rajayoga is achieved through Hathayoga. The commentary then outlines the Seven Stages of Wisdom (Jnanabhumikas) from traditional lore: 1. Subheccha (the initial pure desire for truth, endowed with discrimination and dispassion); 2. Vicarana (inquiry through study and reflection); 3. Tanumanasa (the thinning of the mind through deep contemplation, where the mind flows toward the One); 4. Sattvapatti (the direct realization 'I am Brahman' occurring in a purified inner instrument, representing Samprajnata Samadhi); 5. Asansakti (complete non-attachment to yogic powers, where the yogi awakens spontaneously from Samadhi); 6. Pararthabhavini (where the yogi does not perceive external objects and is awakened only by others); and 7. Turyaga (the state of perpetual abidance in the fourth state, where there is no awakening, also known as Jivanmukti or Svatmarama).

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: शंका: यदि मन्त्रयोग, सगुणध्यान, निर्गुणध्यान और मुद्राओं के द्वारा ही राजयोग की सिद्धि हो सकती है, तो हठविद्या के उपदेश की क्या आवश्यकता है? इस शंका का समाधान करते हुए ग्रन्थकार कहते हैं कि विक्षिप्त चित्त वाले साधकों के लिए हठयोग के द्वारा ही राजयोग की सिद्धि होती है। इसके समर्थन में ज्ञान की सात भूमिकाओं का वर्णन किया गया है: १. शुभेच्छा (विवेक-वैराग्य युक्त तीव्र मुमुक्षुता), २. विचारणा (श्रवण और मनन), ३. तनुमानसा (निदिध्यासन के द्वारा मन की सूक्ष्मता), ४. सत्त्वापत्ति (शुद्ध अन्तःकरण में 'अहं ब्रह्मास्मी' का अपरोक्ष अनुभव, जो सम्प्रज्ञात समाधि है), ५. असंसक्ति (सिद्धियों में आसक्ति न होना, जिसमें योगी स्वयं जाग्रत होता है), ६. परार्थाभाविनी (ब्रह्म के अतिरिक्त अन्य वस्तु का भान न होना, जिसमें योगी दूसरों के जगाने पर जागता है), और ७. तुर्यगा (परम समाधि की स्थिति जहाँ स्वतः या परतः कोई व्युत्थान नहीं होता, जिसे जीवन्मुक्ति या स्वात्माराम पद कहा जाता है)।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Rājayoga and the Stages of Spiritual Wisdom (Jñānabhūmikās)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse addresses the state of seekers who are confused by the overwhelming and conflicting systems of philosophy and practices. It argues that Hathayoga is not a competing path but a necessary physical and mental preparation designed specifically to lead distracted minds toward the state of Rajayoga, which is the highest state of absorption (Samadhi).

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In the modern age of information overload, seekers face a similar 'darkness of conflicting opinions' due to spiritual consumerism. The verse's warning remains highly relevant: without a systematic, grounded practice (like Hatha), purely intellectual debates or high-minded meditations can lead to delusion rather than liberation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pragmatic cultivation of Viveka (discrimination), Vairagya (dispassion), Sravana (systematic listening/study), Manana (deep intellectual reflection), Nididhyasana (uninterrupted contemplation), and Hatha-yogic purification of the subtle body to enable steady absorption.
commentary_faqs.answer: The bhashya maps the pursuit of Rajayoga to the seven Jnanabhumi levels of consciousness. It establishes a developmental taxonomy of liberation: the first three stages are 'Sadhana-bhumikas' (preparatory practices), the fourth 'Sattvapatti' is the 'Phala-bhumi' (attainment of non-dual realization or Samprajnata Samadhi), and the final three stages represent progressive depths of Asamprajnata Samadhi leading to absolute Jivanmukti (Turyaga).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this framework counters 'spiritual bypassing' by showing that mental quietude cannot be forced; it requires systematic progression. The term 'bahumata-dhvanta' perfectly describes the cognitive fatigue and anxiety caused by modern information overload, suggesting that physical-somatic yoga (Hatha) is a necessary stabilizing anchor before attempting advanced mental techniques.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
महत्सेवितत्वाद्धठविद्यां प्रशंसन् स्वस्यापि महत्सकाशाद्धठविद्यालाभाद्गौरवं द्योतयति -
नास्ति बुद्धिरयुक्तस्य न चायुक्तस्य भावना ।
न चाभवयतश्शान्तिः अशान्तस्य कुतस्सुखम् । इति (२.६६)
नारायणतीर्थैरप्युक्तम्-
‘स्वातन्त्र्यसत्यत्वमुखं प्रधाने सत्यं च चिद्भेतगतं च वाक्यैः ।
‘अपि चात्मप्रदं योगं व्याकरोन्मतिमान् स्वयम् ।
मतो योगो भगवता गीतायामधिकोऽन्यतः ।
‘वेदेषु यज्ञेषु तपस्सु चैव दानेषु यत्पुण्यफलं प्रदिष्टम् ।
इति भगवदुक्तेः(भ.गी. ८.२८) । किं बहुना । ‘ जिज्ञासुरपि योगस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते’ इति वदता भगवता (भ.गी. ६.४४) योगजिज्ञासोरपि औत्कृष्ट्यं वर्णितं किमुत योगिनः । नारदादिभक्तश्रेष्ठैःयाज्ञवल्क्यादिज्ञानिमुख्यैश्च अस्याः सेवनात् भक्तज्ञानिनामप्यविरुद्धेत्युपरम्यते ॥ ४ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: By praising Hatha Yoga because it has been practiced by great sages, the author demonstrates the dignity and gravity of this science, which he himself received from a great master. To support this, scriptures and commentaries are quoted: 'There is no steady intellect for the unintegrated, nor is there meditation for him... how can there be happiness without peace?' (Gita 2.66). It is also remarked by Narayana Tirtha that Bhagavan Krishna himself expounded Yoga as superior to other paths in the Gita, declaring that whatever merit is promised in Vedas, sacrifices, or charities, Yoga transcends them all. Bhagavan further states that even a seeker who merely wishes to know Yoga transcends the ritualistic realm of Sabda-Brahman (Gita 6.44)—how much more so a perfected Yogi! Since this path was practiced by foremost devotees like Narada and master-knowers like Yajnavalkya, it is perfectly consistent with both devotion (Bhakti) and wisdom (Jnana).

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: महान पुरुषों द्वारा सेवित होने के कारण हठविद्या की प्रशंसा करते हुए, लेखक अपने गुरु रूपी महान आश्रय से हठविद्या की प्राप्ति होने से इसकी गुरुता और गौरव को प्रकट करते हैं—'अयुक्त (जिसका मन वश में नहीं है) पुरुष की बुद्धि स्थिर नहीं होती, न ही उसमें भावना (ध्यान) होती है... अशान्त को सुख कहाँ?' (गीता २.६६)। नारायण तीर्थ ने भी कहा है कि भगवान ने स्वयं गीता में योग को अन्य साधनों से श्रेष्ठ माना है। भगवान कहते हैं—'वेदों, यज्ञों, तपों और दानों में जो पुण्य फल कहा गया है, योगी उस सब का अतिक्रमण कर जाता है।' (गीता ८.२८)। अधिक क्या कहें, 'योग का जिज्ञासु भी शब्दब्रह्म (वैदिक कर्मकाण्ड) को पार कर जाता है'—ऐसा कहकर भगवान ने योग के साधारण जिज्ञासु की भी महिमा गाई है, तो फिर सिद्ध योगी की महिमा का क्या कहना! नारद जैसे श्रेष्ठ भक्तों और याज्ञवल्क्य जैसे प्रमुख ज्ञानियों द्वारा इसका अभ्यास किए जाने के कारण, यह हठविद्या भक्तों और ज्ञानियों दोनों के लिए पूर्णतः सुसंगत और अविरोधी है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Lineage Transmission and Greatness of Hatha Yoga (Parampara)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse establishes the authenticity of Hatha Yoga by grounding it in a sacred lineage of exalted masters like Matsyendranatha and Gorakshanatha. The accompanying commentary reinforces this by showing that Hatha Yoga is not a modern or isolated invention but a highly revered science praised by scriptures like the Bhagavad Gita and practiced by ancient sages, which leads to mental control, peace, and ultimate self-realization.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In contemporary times, Yoga is often reduced to physical fitness. This verse and its commentary remind practitioners of the spiritual lineage and profound depth of Hatha Yoga, elevating it from a mere physical exercise to an authentic path of self-mastery approved by historical and philosophical giants.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The primary practices indicated here involve 'Yogabhyasa' under a lineage ('Parampara' / 'Mahat-sakashat'), focusing on 'Bhavana' (contemplation/meditation) and 'Indriya-nigraha' (sensory control) to attain 'Shanti' (inner peace) and 'Sukha' (true happiness).
commentary_faqs.answer: The commentary establishes the concept of 'Mahat-sevitattva' (being practiced by great masters) and its integration with 'Bhakti' (devotion) and 'Jnana' (knowledge). It asserts that Hatha Yoga is not a separate materialistic discipline but a foundational, supportive science of spiritual integration (Yoga) that transcends ritualistic Vedic structures ('Sabda-Brahma-ativartana').

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: From a secular and psychological viewpoint, this text addresses the root cause of mental distress—the lack of mental integration ('ayukta') leading to lack of peace ('ashanti'). It highlights that true mental peace and psychological well-being cannot be achieved through external acquisition or ritualistic actions but through systematic internal integration (Yoga), validating the contemporary emphasis on mindfulness and mental fitness.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Guru-Parampara (Lineage of Masters)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse serves as an invocation (Mangalacharana) to the lineage of Hatha Yoga, establishing the authority of the tradition through its primordial masters. By naming these Siddhas, the text anchors itself in a divine transmission that transcends human history.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It emphasizes the importance of lineage in spiritual practices, highlighting that knowledge is not merely intellectual but experiential, transmitted from enlightened masters to disciples.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice revolves around 'Hatha-Vidya'—the specific technological methods of bodily and pranic mastery as passed down through the enumerated lineage.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Siddha-Parampara, where the term 'Aishvarya' in the Bhashya indicates that the mastery of Hatha Yoga leads to both spiritual liberation and the manifestation of Siddhis.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this establishes a 'connective motivation.' By identifying with a successful lineage, practitioners overcome hesitation and doubt, fostering a sense of discipline and belonging in their wellness or meditative journey.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Lineage of Yogic Siddhas
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse lists names associated with a specific tradition of practitioners or Siddhas who have attained mastery. It underscores the importance of the guru-shishya parampara in the transmission of esoteric yogic knowledge.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This reflects the historical tradition in India of documenting lineages of realized beings, reinforcing the notion that spiritual attainment is a shared, inherited, and disciplined path.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices involve internalizing these names or identities within a tantric or yogic meditation framework (nyasa or dhyana).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Siddha-parampara where the names signify specific energetic or archetypal manifestations of the Yogi, acting as a collective identity for the practice.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the archetypal modeling in human learning, where identifying with a lineage or a 'master' model helps in stabilizing the practitioner's own meditative focus and mental discipline.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Guru Bhakti and Siddha Lineage
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes the absolute purity and exalted status of the lineage master, Kaneri, identifying him with the eternal, stainless divinity. By acknowledging the Guru's feet as 'worship-worthy', the practitioner aligns themselves with the source of spiritual light.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This reflects the Indian tradition of honoring the Guru-parampara as an extension of the Divine, which remains vital for transmitting esoteric knowledge in contemporary spiritual lineages.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Guru-stuti (praising the master), constant remembrance (anusmarana) of the Siddha, and recognition of the Guru's stainless (nirañjana) nature.
commentary_faqs.answer: The Bhashya clarifies the epithet 'Kaneri' as referring to the identity of the Siddha 'Kācaṇḍīśvara', establishing a link to a divine archetype of consciousness (caitanya).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this supports the practice of 'idealization' of a mentor, which helps in self-transcendence, shifting the practitioner's identity from limited ego to a broader, 'stainless' or untainted state of awareness.

commentary_faqs.answer: The verse lists names associated with the Viraśaiva or Siddha tradition, acknowledging figures who have attained spiritual mastery. It serves to establish a historical or lineage-based authority (Guru-parampara) for the practices discussed.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This reflects the Indian tradition of honoring lineage, recognizing that profound spiritual knowledge is passed through realized beings who act as conduits for transmission.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Smarana (Remembering the names of the masters/Siddhas as part of respectful homage).
commentary_faqs.answer: Samuccaya-buddhi (The concept of aggregation in listing historical figures to validate a lineage or school of thought).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Acknowledging the role of predecessors in intellectual and spiritual development, fostering a sense of rootedness and continuity in one's personal growth.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: इति पूर्वोक्ता आदयः येषां ते तथा । आदिशब्देन तारानाथादयो ग्राह्याः । महान्तश्च ते सिद्धाश्च अप्रतिहतैश्वर्या इत्यर्थः । हठयोगस्य प्रभावात् सामर्थ्यादिति हठयोगप्रभावतः । पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् । कालो मृत्युः तस्य दण्डनं दण्डः देहप्राणवियोगानुकूलो व्यापारः तं खण्डयित्वा छित्वा मृत्युं जित्वेत्यर्थः । ब्रह्माण्डमध्ये विचरन्ति विशेषेणाव्याहतगत्या चरन्तीत्यर्थः । तदुक्तं भागवते - योगेश्वराणां गतिमाहुरन्तर्बहिस्त्रिलोक्याः पवनान्तरात्मनाम्’ इति ॥ ९ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: ‘These and others’ refers to those mentioned previously. The word ‘ādi’ (etc.) includes masters like Taranatha. ‘Mahasiddhas’ means those who have attained unobstructed divine power (aisvarya). ‘Hathayogaprabhavatah’ means by the force or capability of Hatha Yoga, where the ‘tasil’ suffix indicates the ablative case. Having shattered or severed the ‘danda’ (staff) of death, which refers to the process of separation between body and breath, they have conquered death. They roam within the cosmic egg (brahmanda) moving without any obstruction. As stated in the Bhagavata: ‘They call the path of the masters of Yoga as moving inside and outside the three worlds, through the internal soul of wind (prana).’

commentaries.description: ‘इत्यादयः’ का अर्थ है वे जो पूर्व में कहे गए हैं। ‘आदि’ शब्द से तारानाथ आदि सिद्धों का ग्रहण करना चाहिए। ‘महासिद्धाः’ का अर्थ है वे महान सिद्ध जिनकी ऐश्वर्य शक्ति अप्रतिहत (बाधा रहित) है। ‘हठयोगप्रभावतः’ का अर्थ है हठयोग के सामर्थ्य या प्रभाव से, जहाँ ‘तसिल्’ प्रत्यय पञ्चमी विभक्ति के अर्थ में है। मृत्यु के दण्ड (अर्थात् देह-प्राण वियोग की प्रक्रिया) को खण्डित कर उन्होंने मृत्यु को जीत लिया है। वे ब्रह्माण्ड के भीतर अव्याहत गति से विचरण करते हैं। जैसा कि भागवत में कहा गया है - ‘योगेश्वर प्राण-वायु के माध्यम से तीनों लोकों के भीतर-बाहर विचरण करते हैं’।”

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Siddhi (Spiritual Perfection) through Hatha Yoga
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes that the attainment of supernatural or spiritual mastery is not an accident but a direct result of the disciplined practice of Hatha Yoga. It highlights that the human body can be transformed into a vessel of infinite potential through the systematic control of vital energies.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In contemporary times, this underscores the therapeutic and transformative power of yoga, moving beyond mere physical exercise to suggest that dedicated practice allows individuals to transcend physical limitations and 'conquer' mortality in a symbolic or experiential sense.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Hathayoga practice, Prāṇāyāma (implied by pavana-ātmā), and the pursuit of ‘Aisvarya’ (divine sovereignty).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept explores ‘Mahāsiddhi’ arising from ‘Haṭhayoga’, specifically focusing on the ‘Jaya’ (conquest) over ‘Mṛtyu-daṇḍa’ (the rod of death/separation of soul and body).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: It suggests the psychological potential to overcome the fear of death and the ‘obstructions’ (āvyāhata-gati) in life through the disciplined mastery of one's own internal energy flow (prana).

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Duhkha-nivritti (Cessation of Suffering)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse frames Hatha Yoga not merely as physical postures, but as a sanctuary. It suggests that the practitioner, scorched by the 'tapa' (the three-fold miseries of existence), finds cooling refuge in the disciplined system of Hatha.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this emphasizes Yoga as a therapeutic refuge for mental and physical stress, moving beyond the physical 'asana' into the realm of a protective, life-sustaining system.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Hatha Yoga practice (Āsanavidhi), internal refuge (Samāśraya).
commentary_faqs.answer: Aśeṣatāpanāśakatvam (the nature of destroying all suffering) and Sarvayogasādhakatvam (the capability of accomplishing all Yoga stages).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychological stabilization through somatic regulation. Treating yoga as a safe space for nervous system restoration in a high-stress society.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
अथाखिलविद्यापेक्षया हठविद्याया अतिगोप्यत्वमाह - हठविद्येति । सिद्धिमणिमाद्यैश्वर्यमिच्छता यद्वा सिद्धिं कैवल्यमिच्छता वाञ्छता योगिना हठयोगविद्या परमत्यन्तं गोप्या गोपनीया गोपनार्हास्तीति । तत्र हेतुमाह । यतो गुप्ता हठविद्या वीर्यवती अप्रतिहत-ऐश्वर्यजननसमर्था स्यात् । कैवल्यजननसमर्था कैवल्यसिद्धिजननसमर्था वा स्यात् । प्रकाशिता प्रसिद्धिं गमिता तु निर्वीर्या । दीर्घकालसेवितापि अप्रतिहत- ऐश्वर्यजननसमर्था कैवल्यसिद्धिजननसमर्था वा स्यात् । अथ योगाधिकारी
जिताक्षाय शान्ताय सक्ताय मुक्तौ विहीनाय दोषैरसक्ताय भुक्तौ ।
याज्ञवल्क्यः ।
विध्युक्तकर्मसंयुक्तः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जितः ।
‘कृतविद्यो जितक्रोधः सत्यधर्मपरायणः ।
इति । ‘शिश्नोदररतायैव न देयं वेषधारिणे’ इति कुत्रचित् । अत्र योगचिन्तामणिकारः -
यद्यपि
‘ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां स्त्रीशूद्राणाञ्च पावनम् ।
इत्यादि पुराणवाक्येषु प्राणिमात्रस्य योगेऽधिकार उपलभ्यते, तथापि मोक्षरूपफलवति योगे विरक्तस्यैव अधिकार उचितः । तथा च वायुसंहितायाम् -
‘दृष्टे तथानुश्रविके विरक्तं विषये मनः ।
सुरेश्वराचार्याः -
‘इहामुत्र विरक्तस्य संसारं प्रजिहासतः ।
वृद्धैरप्युक्तम् -
‘नैतद्देयं दुर्विनीताय जातु ज्ञानं गुप्तं तद्धि सम्यक्फलाय ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary explains the importance of secrecy for Hatha Yoga compared to other sciences. It posits that secret knowledge is 'Viryavati' (potent/virile), capable of generating unobstructed excellence or liberation (Kaivalya). If made public, it loses its efficacy. The commentary then quotes Yājñavalkya to define a qualified practitioner: one who has conquered their senses, is peaceful, free from worldly attachments, and avoids desire. It stresses that while Yoga is for all, only those truly detached from worldly and heavenly pleasures are fit for the ultimate goal of Moksha.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: भाष्य स्पष्ट करता है कि अन्य विधाओं की तुलना में हठयोग विद्या का अत्यंत गोपनीय होना आवश्यक है। भाष्य कहता है कि जो विद्या गुप्त रखी जाती है, वही 'वीर्यवती' या प्रभावशाली होती है, जो सिद्धियों और कैवल्य (मोक्ष) को प्रदान करने में समर्थ है। यदि इसे प्रकाशित (सर्वसुलभ) कर दिया जाए, तो यह निर्वीर्य हो जाती है। भाष्य याज्ञवल्क्य के वचनों को उद्धृत कर बताता है कि योग का अधिकार केवल उन्हीं को है जो जितेन्द्रिय, शांत, दोषों से मुक्त और विषयासक्ति से परे हैं।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Gopaniyatā (Secrecy/Confidentiality in Spiritual Practice)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes that the potent techniques of Hatha Yoga operate on subtle energies that require a prepared vessel. Without the shield of secrecy and proper guidance, these energies can lead to dissipation of power or mental agitation, hence the necessity of concealment.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In a modern context, this translates to the requirement of personalized, qualified mentorship rather than learning profound transformative techniques through mass-media or commercialized, superficial platforms which lack the depth of lineage-based tradition.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed qualities for a practitioner: Jitakṣa (conquered senses), Śāntāya (peaceful mind), Kāmasaṅkalpavarjita (devoid of desire and intention), and Vairāgya (detachment).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Gup' (secrecy) is not merely to hide, but to preserve 'Virya' (spiritual potency/potential energy) of the Vidya, ensuring the 'Kaivalya-siddhi' remains protected from the dissipation caused by improper, undisciplined practice (adhikara-bheda).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: From a psychological perspective, this reflects the principle of cognitive integration and spiritual maturity. The 'secrecy' ensures that the individual's psyche is sufficiently robust and stable before engaging with powerful psycho-somatic technologies, preventing ego-inflation or emotional imbalance.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
अथ हठाभ्यासयोग्यंं देशमाह सार्धेन -
एकान्ते विजने । अनेन जनसमागमाभावात् कलहाद्यभावः सूचितः । जनसम्मर्दे तु कलहादिकं स्यादेव । तदुक्तं भागवते - ‘वासे बहूनां कलहो भवेद्वार्ता द्वयोरपि’ इति ।
तादृशे मठिकामध्ये । अल्पः मठः मठिका । अल्पीयसि कन् । तस्याः मध्ये हठयोगिना हठाभ्यासी योगी हठयोगी तेन । शाकपार्थिवादिवत् समासः । स्थातव्यं स्थातुं योग्यम् । मठिकामध्य इत्यनेन शीतातपादिजनितक्लेशाभावः सूचितः । अत्र ‘युक्ताहारविहारेण हठयोगस्य सिद्धये’ इत्यर्धं केनचित् क्षिप्तत्वात् न व्याख्यातम् । मूलश्लोकानामेव व्याख्यानम् । एवमग्रेऽपि ये मया न व्यख्याताः श्लोकाः हठप्रदीपिकायामुपलभ्येरन् ते सर्वेऽपि क्षिप्ता इति बोद्धव्यम् ॥ १२ ॥
commentaries.text:
अथ हठाभ्यासयोग्यंं देशमाह सार्धेन -
एकान्ते विजने । अनेन जनसमागमाभावात् कलहाद्यभावः सूचितः । जनसम्मर्दे तु कलहादिकं स्यादेव । तदुक्तं भागवते - ‘वासे बहूनां कलहो भवेद्वार्ता द्वयोरपि’ इति ।
तादृशे मठिकामध्ये । अल्पः मठः मठिका । अल्पीयसि कन् । तस्याः मध्ये हठयोगिना हठाभ्यासी योगी हठयोगी तेन । शाकपार्थिवादिवत् समासः । स्थातव्यं स्थातुं योग्यम् । मठिकामध्य इत्यनेन शीतातपादिजनितक्लेशाभावः सूचितः । अत्र ‘युक्ताहारविहारेण हठयोगस्य सिद्धये’ इत्यर्धं केनचित् क्षिप्तत्वात् न व्याख्यातम् । मूलश्लोकानामेव व्याख्यानम् । एवमग्रेऽपि ये मया न व्यख्याताः श्लोकाः हठप्रदीपिकायामुपलभ्येरन् ते सर्वेऽपि क्षिप्ता इति बोद्धव्यम् ॥ १२ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Now, the author describes the place suitable for the practice of Hatha Yoga with one and a half verses. 'Ekante vijane' means a secluded and lonely place. By this, the absence of conflicts due to the lack of human congregation is indicated. Where there is a crowd, conflict is inevitable; as it is said in the Bhagavata, 'Where there are many living together, there is conflict; even with two, there is talk.' In such a 'Mathika' (a small hermitage/hut); 'Mathika' is a small monastery. By this (the choice of such a place), the absence of suffering caused by cold, heat, etc., is implied. Note: The author mentions that certain half-verses found in other editions of the Hatha Pradipika are interpolations and are therefore not commented upon.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: अब हठाभ्यास के योग्य देश को सार्ध श्लोक (डेढ़ श्लोक) द्वारा बताते हैं। एकान्त और विजन स्थान का अर्थ है ऐसा स्थान जहाँ जन-समागम न हो। इससे कलह के अभाव की सूचना दी गई है। जनसमूह में तो कलह निश्चित ही है। भागवत में भी कहा है - 'बहुओं के वास में कलह होती है, यहाँ तक कि दो के बीच में भी बातचीत से विक्षेप होता है।' ऐसी मठिका (छोटी कुटी) के मध्य में योगी को ठहरना चाहिए। इससे शीतातपादि (ठंड, गर्मी आदि) से उत्पन्न क्लेशों का अभाव सूचित होता है। यहाँ 'युक्ताहारविहारेण...' आदि अर्ध-श्लोकों को प्रक्षिप्त मानकर उनकी व्याख्या नहीं की गई है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Deśa-kāla-pātra (Environmental suitability for Yoga)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes that the external environment directly affects internal stability. A yogi requires a stable, peaceful, and secure physical environment to minimize sensory distraction and ensure the continuity of their practice.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern terms, this underscores the importance of a 'conducive setting' for mental health and deep work, acknowledging that societal and physical security is a prerequisite for higher intellectual and spiritual growth.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribes 'Ekānta-vāsā' (living in seclusion) and choosing a 'Maṭhikā' (a small, sheltered space) to minimize 'upadrava' (external and internal disturbances).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept focuses on 'Deśa-vikalpa' (selection of space) where 'nirupadravatva' (absence of turbulence) acts as a catalyst for 'citta-prasādana' (tranquility of mind) as per Hatha-yoga frameworks.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Reflects the psychological need for 'safe spaces' and 'sensory regulation' in a hyper-stimulated digital age, emphasizing that environmental stability is the foundation of cognitive focus and mindfulness.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
अथ मठलक्षणमाह -
अत्युच्चं च तन्नीचं च अत्युच्चनीचं, तच्च तदायतं च अत्युच्चनीचायतम् । ‘विशेषणं विशेष्येण बहुलं’ (पा.सू २.१.५७) इत्यत्र बहुलग्रहणात् विशेषणानां कर्मधारयः ।
ननु उच्चनीचायतशब्दानां भिन्नार्थकानां कथं कर्मधारयः? ‘तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः’ (पा.सू १.२.४२) इति तल्लक्षणादिति चेत्, न । मठे तेषां सामानााधिकरण्यसम्भवात् । न अत्युच्चनीचायतं नात्युच्चनीचायतं, नशब्देन समासान्नलोपाभावः, नेति पृथक्पदं वा । अत्युच्चे आरोहणे श्रमः स्यादतिनीचेऽवरोहणे श्रमो भवेत् । अत्यायते दूरं दृष्टिर्गच्छेत्, तन्निराकरणार्थमुक्तं नात्युच्चनीचायतमिति । सम्यक् समीचीनतया गोमयेन गोपुरीषेण सान्द्रं यथा भवति तथा लिप्तम् । अमलं निर्मलम् । निःशेषा निखिला ये जन्तवः मशकमत्कुणाद्याः तैरुज्झितं त्यक्तं रहितम् । बाह्ये मठाद्बहिः प्रदेशे । मण्डपः शालाविशेषः, वेदिः परिष्कृता भूमिः कूपो जलाशयविशेषः, तैः रुचिरं रमणीयम् । प्राकारेण वरणेन सम्यग्वेष्टितं परितो भित्तियुक्तमित्यर्थः । हठाभ्यासिभिः हठयोगाभ्यसनशीलैः सिद्धैः । इदं पूर्वोक्तमल्पद्वारादिकं योगमठस्य लक्षणं स्वरूपं प्रोक्तं कथितम् ।
नन्दोकेश्वरपुराणे त्वेवं मठलक्षणमुक्तम् -
मन्दिरं रम्यविन्यासं मनोज्ञं गन्धवासितम् ।
धूपामोदादिसुरभि कुसुमोत्करमण्डितम् ।
मुनितीर्थनदीवृक्षपद्मिनीशैलशोभितम् ।
चित्रकर्मनिबद्धं च चित्रभेदविचित्रितम् ।
कुर्याद् योगगृहं धीमान् सुरम्यं शुभवर्त्मना ।
दृष्ट्वा चित्रगतांश्छान्तान् मुनीन् याति मनःशामम् ।
सिद्धान् दृष्ट्वा चित्रगतान् मतिरभ्युद्यमे भवेत् ।
मध्ये योगगृहस्याथ लिखेत् संसारमण्डलम् ।
श्मशानं च महाघोरं नरकांश्च लिखेत् क्वचित् ।
तान् दृष्ट्वा भीषणाकारान् संसारे सारवर्जिते ।
अनवसादो भवति योगी सिद्ध्यभिलाषुकः ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary defines the characteristics of a Matha (yoga cell). It explains 'atyuccanīcāyatam' as a compound analyzing height and dimensions, noting that extreme height causes fatigue during climbing, and extreme depth causes fatigue during descent. Excessive expanse causes the eyes to wander too far. Thus, the text prescribes a balanced structure to avoid sensory and physical distraction. It further notes the necessity of a clean, secluded, and well-enclosed space, as supported by the Nandeswara Purana, which suggests that the visual environment of the yoga cell (art, beauty, and representations of reality) serves to stabilize the mind of the yogi.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: टीका में मठ के लक्षणों का वर्णन है। 'अत्युच्चनीचायतम्' की व्याख्या करते हुए कहा गया है कि अधिक ऊँचाई चढ़ने में और अधिक गहराई उतरने में थकान पैदा करती है। अत्यधिक विस्तृत स्थान दृष्टि को दूर तक भटकाता है। अतः, शारीरिक और मानसिक व्याकुलता से बचने के लिए मध्यम आकार का स्थान उचित है। नन्दिकेश्वर पुराण के अनुसार, योग-स्थान का वातावरण रमणीय, सुगंधित और एकाग्रता बढ़ाने वाला होना चाहिए, जहाँ योगी वैराग्य और सिद्धि के प्रति प्रेरित हो सके।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Environment for Yoga (Matha-lakshana)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse establishes the physical prerequisites for a meditation space, emphasizing moderation and seclusion. A controlled, balanced environment minimizes external sensory stimulation and prevents physical discomfort, thereby fostering internal concentration (Ekagrata).

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this emphasizes the importance of 'ergonomic' and 'mindful' living spaces. It suggests that our physical surroundings directly influence our mental state, advocating for simplicity and freedom from distraction.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Vairagya (dispassion), Ekantha-vasa (solitude), and Yoga-shala-nirmana (cultivating a focused space).
commentary_faqs.answer: Sthala-shuddhi and Mana-nirodha (External environment as a catalyst for internal state, preventing Vikshepa or sensory dissipation).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychology of space: Designing personal environments that reduce cognitive load and sensory clutter, facilitating 'flow' states and mindfulness in a high-stimulus digital world.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
मठलक्षणमुक्त्वा मठे यत् कर्तव्यं तदाह
मरुज्जयो यस्य सिद्धस्तं सेवेत गुरुं सदा ।
राजयोगे -
वेदान्ततर्कोक्तिभिरागमैश्च नानाविधैः शस्त्रकदम्बकैश्च ।
स्कन्दपुराराणे-
आचार्याद्योगसर्वस्वम् अवाप्य स्थिरधीः स्वयम् ।
सुरेश्वराचार्यः -
गुरुप्रसादाल्लभते योगमष्टाङ्गसंयुतम् ।
शिवप्रसादाल्लभते योगसिद्धिं च शाश्वतीम् ।
श्रुतिश्च -
“यस्य देवे परा भक्तिः यथा देवे तथा गुरौ ।
आचार्यवान् पुरुषो वेद इति च (छां.उप.६.१४.२) ॥ १४ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Having defined the characteristics of the monastery (maṭha), the text now describes what must be done there: One should always serve the Guru who has mastered the control of prana (marut-jaya). As stated in the Rajayoga: through Vedantic reasoning, diverse scriptures, and various analytical texts. In the Skanda Purana: Having obtained the essence of Yoga from the Acharya, one becomes steady-minded. Sureshwaracharya says: Through the grace of the Guru, one attains the eight-limbed yoga; through the grace of Shiva, one attains eternal perfection in yoga. The Shruti (Chhandogya Upanishad 6.14.2) also confirms: 'To one who has a Guru, knowledge is revealed.'

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: मठ के लक्षणों का वर्णन करने के पश्चात, अब वहाँ क्या करना चाहिए यह बताते हैं: जिस गुरु ने मरुज्जय (प्राण-नियंत्रण) सिद्ध कर लिया हो, उसकी सदा सेवा करनी चाहिए। राजयोग में कहा है - वेदान्त के तर्कों, नाना प्रकार के आगमों और विविध शास्त्रों के माध्यम से (ज्ञान प्राप्त करें)। स्कन्द पुराण में कहा है - आचार्य से योग का सर्वस्व प्राप्त कर साधक स्थिर बुद्धि वाला बनता है। सुरेश्वराचार्य कहते हैं - गुरु की कृपा से अष्टांग योग प्राप्त होता है और शिव की कृपा से शाश्वती योगसिद्धि मिलती है। श्रुति भी कहती है - आचार्यवान् पुरुष ही सत्य को जानता है (छांदोग्य उपनिषद ६.१४.२)।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Ekantavasa and Chitta-shuddhi (Seclusion and Mental Purification)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse highlights the necessity of environmental stability (maṭha) as a prerequisite for internal stability. By dwelling in a conducive space, the practitioner is able to abandon the mental clutter of worldly concerns, which is essential for deep meditative absorption.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In the modern context, this emphasizes the importance of 'psychological space' and 'digital detoxification'. Just as the ancient yogin sought a monastery to escape noise, modern individuals need physical and mental boundaries to maintain mental hygiene amidst constant information overload.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Seclusion in a conducive environment, rendering service to the Guru (Guru-sevana), and the study of Vedantic texts and Agamas.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on Guru-parampara and the role of the Guru as the essential catalyst for Yogic success (Yoga-siddhi) and the removal of mental disturbances (Chitta-vivarjana).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this reinforces the need for mentorship and focused learning environments. It highlights that self-improvement requires both an external framework of discipline and an internal surrender to higher wisdom, countering the modern myth of purely self-taught success.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Obstacles to Yoga (Yoga-pratibandhaka)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse identifies behavioral pitfalls that dissipate the vital energy required for spiritual practice. By highlighting moderation (Yukta-ahara) and flexibility, it emphasizes that yoga is a balanced state of being rather than a regime of extremes.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In the modern era, these 'obstacles' mirror the distractions of over-consumption, burnout, information overload, and rigid perfectionism. It serves as a reminder that wellness is rooted in equilibrium rather than obsessive discipline.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Cultivation of 'Mita-ahara' (moderate diet), 'Yukta-cheshta' (balanced activity), and 'Sattva-shuddhi' (purity of intention through mental flexibility).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept addresses 'Yogapratibandhaka' (obstacles to union) which hinder the 'Abhyasa' (consistent practice) by causing 'Vikshepa' (mental dissipation).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this verse warns against 'orthorexia' and 'over-optimization' syndrome, encouraging a sustainable path that avoids both sensory excess and rigid psychological conditioning.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Yogasiddhi (Success in Yoga)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse outlines the foundational psychological and spiritual pillars required to achieve mastery in any discipline, especially Yoga. It suggests that success is not accidental but the result of a specific cultivation of mental strength and intellectual clarity.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These virtues remain highly relevant in modern goal-setting, professional development, and emotional intelligence, representing the intersection between ancient spiritual discipline and contemporary personal growth.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practices prescribed are the cultivation of enthusiasm (Utsāha), boldness (Sāhasa), endurance (Dhairya), and philosophical discernment (Tattvajñāna).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept addresses the essential qualities for 'Yogasiddhi' (perfection in yoga), which include 'Tattvajñāna' (metaphysical knowledge) and 'Niścaya' (firm resolve).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this verse emphasizes the role of resilience and grit. In secular terms, it highlights how cognitive clarity and emotional regulation are precursors to professional and personal peak performance.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
आदावासनकथने सङ्गतिं सामान्यतः तत्फलं चाह
प्रत्याहारादिसमाध्यन्तानां नादानुसन्धानेऽन्तर्भावः । तन्मध्ये आसनस्य प्रथमाङ्गत्वात्, पूर्वमासनमुच्यत इति सम्बन्धः । तदासनं स्थैर्यं देहस्य मनश्चाञ्चल्यरूप-रजोधर्म- नाशकत्वेन स्थिरतां कुर्यात् । ‘आसनेन रजो हन्ति’ इति वाक्यात् । आरोग्यं चित्तविक्षेपक- रोगाभावः । रोगस्य चित्तविक्षेपकत्वमुक्तं पातञ्जलसूत्रे - ‘व्याधिस्त्यानसंशयप्रमाद- आलस्याविरतिभ्रान्तिदर्शनालब्धभूमिकत्वानवस्थितत्वानि चित्तविक्षेपाः तेऽन्तरायाः’ इति (यो.सू १.३०) । अङ्गानां लाघवं लघुत्वम् । गौरवरूपतमोधर्मनाशकत्वम् अप्येतेनोक्तम् ।
चकारात् क्षुद्वृद्ध्यादिकमपि बोध्यम् ॥ १७ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Introducing the topic of Asana, the commentator explains the logical sequence and its utility. Practices like Pratyahara through Samadhi are essentially sub-types of Nadanusandhana (focusing on the inner sound). Asana is mentioned first as it is the primary limb. Asana provides stability, destroying the Rajasic quality of mental restlessness. As stated: 'Through Asana, one destroys Rajas.' Health (Arogya) is the absence of diseases that disturb the mind. The Yoga Sutra (1.30) defines such distractions as Vyadhi (disease), Styana (apathy), etc. Lightness (Laghava) refers to physical ease, which also implies the destruction of Tamasic heaviness. The use of 'ca' (and) implies the inclusion of an increase in digestive fire and other benefits.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: आसन कथन के प्रारंभ में, भाष्यकार इसकी संगति और फल का वर्णन करते हैं। प्रत्याहारादि से लेकर समाधि तक के अभ्यास वस्तुतः नादानुसन्धान के ही अंतर्गत आते हैं। चूँकि आसन प्रथम अंग है, इसलिए पहले आसन का कथन किया गया है। आसन देह में स्थिरता प्रदान करता है और मन की चंचलता रूप रजोगुण का नाश करता है। कहा गया है - 'आसनेन रजो हन्ति'। 'आरोग्य' का अर्थ है चित्त को विक्षेपित करने वाले रोगों का अभाव। पतञ्जलि योगसूत्र (१.३०) में व्याधि आदि को चित्त का विक्षेप बताया गया है। अंगों का लाघव अर्थात् हल्कापन, जिससे तमोगुण का नाश भी सिद्ध होता है। 'च'कार का अर्थ है कि इससे जठराग्नि की वृद्धि आदि भी समझना चाहिए।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Ashtanga Yoga Foundations
commentary_faqs.answer: Yama and Niyama serve as the ethical and moral bedrock of yogic practice. They function to purify the practitioner's interactions with the external world and internal psychological states, which is essential before advancing to meditative practices.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In the modern era, these provide a framework for stress management, integrity, and ethical conduct, serving as a psychological foundation for emotional stability and social harmony.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The text prescribes the practice of Asana for the cultivation of Sthairya (steadiness) and Arogya (health), which are requisite conditions for attaining deeper states of Samadhi and Nadanusandhana.
commentary_faqs.answer: The commentary highlights the progression of Yoga where Asana (physical posture) is foundational, serving to mitigate the Guna-based fluctuations of the mind—specifically Rajas (restlessness) and Tamas (heaviness/lethargy). It integrates Hatha Yoga terminology with the Patanjala Yoga Sutra's definition of Chitta-Vikshepa (mental distractions).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: The psychological interpretation of 'health' as the removal of 'mind-disturbing factors' mirrors modern psychosomatic medicine. It suggests that physiological stability (via posture and health) is the primary intervention for cognitive and emotional clarity.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Parampara (Lineage and Authority)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse establishes the legitimacy of yogic postures (asanas) by anchoring them in the tradition of ancient sages and realized yogis. It asserts that these practices are not experimental but have been validated by historical masters.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It emphasizes the importance of lineage in spiritual practice, suggesting that authentic knowledge is passed down through accomplished practitioners who have mastered the techniques themselves.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practice involves the selection and performance of 'Śreṣṭhāsanāni' (excellent postures) sanctioned by the traditional lineage.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on 'Āsana-prāmāṇya' (validity of postures) derived from 'Āpta-vacana' (testimony of authoritative beings) within the Yoga tradition.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern relevance lies in validating physical health practices through evidence-based history and acknowledging the wisdom of long-standing traditions to prevent the distortion of original health techniques.

ऊरुजङ्घान्तराधाय प्रपदे जानुमध्यगे ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Regarding the ease of performance, the author first speaks of Svastikasana: 'Janurvoriti'. 'Janu' implies the knee, and 'Uru' implies the thigh. Here, the word 'Janu' should be understood to include the calf region near the knee. The reading 'Janghorvoriti' (placing between the calf and thigh) is actually better. Having placed both soles of the feet in the space between those (the thighs and calves), keeping the body straight, the yogis call this posture 'Svastika'. Sridhara has stated: 'Placing the forefoot between the thighs and the calves, and the knees in the middle'.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Asana-Vidhi (Methodology of Posture)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse delineates the physical mechanics of Svastikasana, emphasizing the importance of bodily geometry in yogic practice. By placing the feet between the knees and thighs, the practitioner creates a stable foundation (Sthira) for the flow of Prana.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this emphasizes the alignment of the human frame for mental stability and meditation, transcending mere exercise to become a tool for psychological grounding.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practice is Svastikasana, requiring 'Rju-kaya' (erect posture) and 'Samakaya' (balanced body).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on 'Sthirata' (stability) within 'Asana', where the physical body serves as the 'yantra' for internal concentration, requiring precise placement of the limbs (Anga-nyasa).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: From a psychological and physiological perspective, this alignment induces 'neuro-muscular relaxation', facilitating a parasympathetic state conducive to mindfulness and stress reduction.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Posture (Asana)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the precise physical positioning required for Gomukhasana. By crossing the limbs in this specific geometric configuration, the practitioner balances the Hatha yoga energy channels.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It remains a foundational posture in modern therapeutic yoga for improving flexibility in the hips, shoulders, and spine, emphasizing the alignment of the physical body as a vehicle for internal discipline.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice involves the deliberate manipulation of joints (gulpham) and lateral alignment of the lower body, categorized as an essential asana for seated meditation.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept defined here is Gomukhasana (cow-faced pose) which requires specific anatomical placement (niyojayet) to achieve a state of physical stability (sthirata).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: From a modern psychological perspective, such body-mind alignment practices reduce sympathetic nervous system arousal, fostering a grounded, meditative state useful for managing contemporary stress.

commentary_faqs.answer: The verse delineates the physical mechanics of 'Virasana', emphasizing the necessity of physical stability as a foundational requirement for meditation. By placing the foot on the opposite thigh, the practitioner achieves a symmetrical distribution of weight that discourages movement during internal practice.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern life, this posture serves as a somatic bridge between physical health—improving circulation and hip flexibility—and mental discipline, helping the practitioner cultivate focus in a sedentary-oriented modern environment.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Virasana (Hero Pose), involving precise positioning of the pada (foot) on the ūru (thigh) to maintain anatomical equilibrium.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Virasana signifies sthairya (stability) in the physiological structure to support Dhyana (meditation), where the physical alignment acts as a vyakhyana for the stillness of the mind.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, the deliberate act of settling into a steady posture functions as a 'pattern interrupt' for the high-anxiety, hyper-stimulated modern state of mind, signaling the nervous system to transition into a parasympathetic 'rest and digest' mode.

commentaries.description: It describes the Kurmasana: 'Gudam' etc. Having blocked or controlled the anus with the ankles, and having been properly placed (seated) in a reverse order (crossing the feet), this is known as Kurmasana; thus, those who know yoga understand it.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Asana Vidhi (Hatha Yoga Physiology)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the physical mechanics of Kurmasana, where the practitioner uses the pressure of the ankles against the perineum to regulate the Mula-bandha. By establishing this specific posture, the practitioner creates a physical lock that stabilizes the mind and channels the Prana effectively.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern yoga practice, this technique emphasizes the integration of physical alignment with internal focus, highlighting that postures are not merely stretches but instruments for psychological regulation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practices are physical positioning of the ankles (gulpha-nirodha) and maintaining steady concentration (samahita).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Kurmasana involves the Mula-bandha where the physical compression by the gulphau (ankles) serves to control the apana-vayu and prepare the practitioner for steady meditation.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, the practice fosters proprioceptive awareness and the ability to find stillness in physical tension, mirroring the process of emotional containment and cognitive stability.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: कुक्कुटासनमाह - पद्नासनं त्विति । पद्मासनं तु ऊर्वोरिपरि उत्तानचरणस्थापनरूपं सम्यक् स्थापयित्वा । जानुपदेन जानुसन्निहितो जङ्घाप्रदेशः । तच्च ऊरुश्च जानूरू, तयोरन्तरे मध्ये करौ निवेश्य भूमौ संस्थाप्य । करवित्यत्रापि संबध्यते । व्योमस्थं खस्थं पद्मासनसदृशं यत्तत् कुक्कुटासनम् ॥ २३ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Describing Kukkutasana - 'Padmasanam tu...' means: Having properly established the Padmasana, which is the form of placing the soles of the feet upwards upon the thighs. The word 'janu' refers to the calf region near the knee. 'Januru' refers to both the thighs and the knees. Having placed the hands in the space between those two and resting them on the ground, the hands are to be held there. That which is suspended in the air (vyomastam), fixed in space (khastham), resembling the lotus posture, is known as Kukkutasana.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Postural Mechanics
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse initiates the procedure for Kukkutasana, emphasizing that steady seated posture (Padmasana) is the essential foundation for advanced somatic practices. By integrating the limbs in a specific configuration, the practitioner stabilizes the body and directs internal energy (Prana).

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These classical postures continue to serve as the bedrock for modern yoga, emphasizing body-mind control, structural balance, and the intentional preparation of the nervous system for meditation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practices are Padmasana, deliberate limb-placement (janūrvorantare karau), and the final suspension of the body (vyomastam/khastham) to achieve the Kukkutasana state.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on 'sthiti' (stability) and 'vinyasa' (placing), where the body is transformed into a geometric vessel (Kukkutasana) to cultivate control over gravity and physical balance.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychological health benefits include enhanced proprioception, core strength, and the ability to maintain focus under physically challenging conditions (stress inoculation).

commentaries.description: Introducing Uttānakūrmāsana - 'Kukkutāsane...'. Situated in the lock of the Kukkutāsana previously described in the verse, one should bind the neck with both arms. Because one becomes like an upturned tortoise, this pose is named Uttānakūrmakam.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Haṭhayoga Posture (Uttānakūrmāsana)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the transition from Kukkutāsana to Uttānakūrmāsana. It emphasizes the necessity of physical stability and anatomical binding to facilitate the inner containment of energy (Prāṇa) within the yogic body.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern practice, these postures represent the evolution of body-mind control. The physical 'binding' serves as a metaphor for the discipline required to turn the senses inward, moving from external posture to internal stillness.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Kukkutāsana (the prerequisite posture), binding the neck with the arms, and maintaining the supine/upturned position.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Utānakūrmāsana (the upturned tortoise posture), involving the stabilization of physical binding (Bandha) to achieve physiological and meditative stillness.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: This serves as a psychological exercise in structural integrity and flexibility, teaching the practitioner to find comfort and stillness even in complex, constrained physical states.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Describing the Dhanurasana (Bow Pose) - 'pādāṅguṣṭhau tu...'. One should hold the big toes of the feet with the hands and pull them up to the ears just as one pulls a bowstring. The meaning is: keep one arm straight while holding the toe, and retract the other arm holding the other toe up to the ear. This is called Dhanurasana.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga / Asana
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the mechanics of Dhanurasana (Bow Pose), emphasizing the rhythmic tension required to simulate a bowstring. It represents the union of physical discipline with mental focus, where the body's posture mimics a weapon to signify control over one's internal state.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: Dhanurasana is a foundational posture in modern yoga, widely practiced for spinal health, flexibility, and stimulating the digestive system, reflecting the timeless intersection of ancient anatomy and modern wellness.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is 'gṛhītvā' (grasping) and 'ākuñcita' (retracting/folding) to achieve 'śravaṇānta' (ear-level reach), fostering body awareness and spinal alignment.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept defined is Dhanurasana, specifically exploring the 'ākarṣaṇa' (stretching/attraction) movement, which mimics the elasticity of a bow (dhanu), symbolizing the tension between static grounding and active elongation.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern relevance lies in the psychosomatic regulation achieved through intentional postural tension, providing therapeutic relief for sedentary lifestyles, improving posture, and increasing respiratory capacity.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: मत्स्येन्द्रासनमाह - वामोरुमूलेऽर्पितः स्थापितो यो दक्षपादः तं सम्प्रदायात् पृष्ठतोगतवामपणिना गुल्फस्योपरिभागे प्रगृह्य । जानोः दक्षिणपादजानोः बहिः प्रदेशे वेष्टितो यो वामपादस्तं वामपादजानोः बहिर्वेष्टितदक्षिण अङ्गुष्ठे प्रगृह्य । परिवर्तित्ताङ्गः वामभागेन पृष्ठतो मुखं यथा स्यादेवं परिवर्तितं परावर्तितमङ्गं येन स तथा तादृशो यत्र तिष्ठेत् स्थितिं कुर्यात् तदासनं मत्स्येन्द्रनाथोदितं कथितं स्यात् । तदुदितत्वात् तन्नामकमेव वदन्ति । एवं दक्षोरुमूलार्पितवामपादं पृष्ठतोगतदक्षिणपाणिना प्रगृह्य वामजानोः बहिः वेष्टितदक्षपादं दक्षिणपादजानोः बहिः वेष्टितवामपाणिना प्रगृह्य, दक्षभागेन पृष्ठतो मुखं यथास्याद् एवं परिवर्तिताङ्गः च अभ्यसेत् ॥ २७ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Describing Matsyendrasana: Place the right foot at the root of the left thigh. By tradition, grasp the ankle with the right hand passing behind the back. The left foot, wrapped outside the right knee, should be held by the left hand. With the body twisted, face towards the back on the left side; the posture in which one stays like this is called Matsyendrasana (posture taught by Matsyendranatha). One should practice it by reversing the sides as well, grasping the left foot placed at the root of the right thigh with the left hand, and holding the right foot wrapped outside the left knee with the right hand, turning the body towards the right.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: मत्स्येन्द्रासन का कथन है: वाम ऊरु के मूल में अर्पित (स्थित) दक्षिण पाद को, सम्प्रदाय के अनुसार पीछे की ओर ले गए दक्षिण हस्त से टखने (गुल्फ) को पकड़ें। घुटने के बाहर लपेटे गए वाम पाद को वाम हस्त से पकड़ें। शरीर को घुमाकर पीछे की ओर मुख करके जिस स्थिति में बैठें, वह मत्स्येन्द्रनाथ द्वारा कथित 'मत्स्येन्द्रासन' है। इसी प्रकार दक्षिण ऊरु के मूल में वाम पाद को रखकर, पीछे की ओर ले गए वाम हस्त से उसे पकड़ें, और घुटने के बाहर स्थित दक्षिण पाद को दक्षिण हस्त से पकड़कर, दाहिनी ओर शरीर घुमाकर अभ्यास करें।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Posture (Asana)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the precise physical configuration of the Matsyendrasana, a seminal posture in Hatha Yoga. It emphasizes the concept of 'Veshtana' (wrapping or torsion), which is essential for stimulating the spine and internal organs.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: Matsyendrasana is widely practiced today as a primary spinal twist, renowned for its ability to massage abdominal viscera, improve digestion, and maintain spinal flexibility in a sedentary modern lifestyle.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practice includes the specific sequencing of 'Arpana' (placement) and 'Veshtana' (wrapping), concluding with 'Parivartita' (spinal twist).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is 'Parivartita-anga' (torsion of the body) which facilitates spinal alignment, utilizing the 'Kevala' style of limb locking described as 'Veshtana'.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this asana serves as a tool for grounding and 'centering' through physical torsion, while secularly, it is a proven therapeutic modality for alleviating chronic back pain and stimulating the parasympathetic nervous system.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: मत्स्येन्द्रासनस्य फलमाह - मत्स्येन्द्रेति । प्रचण्डं दुस्सहं रुजां रोगाणां मण्डलं समूहः तस्य खण्डने छेदने अस्त्रम् अस्त्रमिव तादृशं मत्स्येन्द्रपीठं मत्स्येन्द्रासनम् । अभ्यासतः प्रत्यहमावर्तनरूपाभ्यासात् पुंसां जठरस्य जठराग्नेः प्रकृष्टां दीप्तिं वृद्धिं ददाति । तथा कुण्डलिन्याः आधारशक्तेः प्रबोधं निद्राभावं तथा चन्द्रस्य तालुनः उपरिभागे स्थितस्य नित्यं क्षरतः स्थिरत्वं क्षरणाभावं च ददातीत्यर्थः ॥ २७ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The text explains the fruits of Matsyendrasana. 'Prachanda' means unbearable; 'Rugmandala' means the host or group of diseases. It is like an 'Astram' (weapon) for the destruction or breaking of such diseases. By regular practice, it gives intense stimulation to the 'Jatharagni' (gastric fire). It also grants the awakening of the Kundalini, the base energy, and brings stability to the nectar of the moon (Chandra) which constantly drips from the palate, preventing its dissipation.
