commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Physiology
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse emphasizes the dual benefit of Matsyendrasana: the physical metabolic activation (Jatharagni) and the therapeutic destruction of systemic illness. It highlights the Hatha Yoga view that physical health is the foundational prerequisite for higher spiritual progress.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this verse bridges the gap between traditional yogic practice and medical well-being, illustrating how specific postures serve as a non-invasive intervention for digestive and chronic metabolic disorders.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Daily practice (Abhyasa), steady physical posture (Asana-sthairya), and the intentional focusing of attention on the digestive center and the palate.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Deha-Siddhi (attainment of a healthy body) via Agni-Dipana (kindling the digestive fire) and Amrit-Sthairya (stabilizing the cooling lunar nectar), where the posture acts as a Jiva-Prakoshthika or a tool for energetic refinement.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: From a psychosomatic perspective, the practice represents a stress-reduction technique that impacts the enteric nervous system, alleviating digestive issues while providing a grounding effect on the autonomic nervous system.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: पश्चिमतानासनमाह - प्रसार्येति । भुवि भूमौ दण्डस्य रूपमिव रूपं ययोः तौ दण्डाकारौ श्लिष्टगुल्फौ प्रसार्य प्रसारितौ कृत्वा । दोर्भ्याम्् आकुञ्चिततर्जनीभ्यां भुजाभ्यां पदोः पदयोः च अग्रे अग्रभागौ तयोर्द्वितयं द्वयमङ्गुष्ठप्रदेशयुग्ममं बलादाकर्षणपूर्वकं यथा जान्वधोभागस्य भूमेरुत्थानं न स्यात् तथा गृहीत्वा । जानोरुपरि न्यस्तो ललाटदेशो येन तादृशो यत्र वसेत् । इदं पश्चिमताननामकम् आसनमाहुः ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The text explains Paschimottanasana. 'Prasarya' means having stretched out. 'Dandarupau' refers to legs that are like a staff—straight and stiff, placed on the ground. 'Dorbhyam' refers to the arms with folded index fingers grasping the feet. 'Padagradvitayam' refers to the pair of toes/front part of the feet. One must grasp them with force such that the knees do not lift off the ground. The forehead should be placed upon the knees. This is known as Paschimottanasana.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Haṭhayoga - Asana
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the foundational physical technique of Paschimottanasana, emphasizing the alignment of the body as a 'danda' (straight staff). It represents the controlled stretching of the spinal column and posterior muscles to prepare the body for pranayama and internal awareness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: Today, this posture is widely recognized for its therapeutic efficacy in spinal health, stress reduction, and stimulating the digestive system, bridging ancient physiological knowledge with modern wellness practices.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice involves 'Dandakara' (straightening like a staff) posture, 'Gṛhītvā' (clasping the feet), and 'Baladakarṣaṇa' (forceful traction) to ensure 'Janu-Bhumi-Samyama' (knees remaining on the ground).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Paschimottanasana' involves the 'Prasaraṇa' (stretching) of the 'Paścima' (back/posterior) portion of the body, which symbolically represents the channel for Pranic flow.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this asana promotes 'Pratyahara' (withdrawal of senses) by focusing the practitioner on the internal sensations of the back body, serving as a grounding technique to counteract the modern sedentary hunched posture.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Haṭhayoga and Prāṇāyāma
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse describes the physiological effect of the Paścimatāna posture, suggesting that it influences the direction of Prāṇa towards the central channel. By stretching the posterior, the yogi facilitates the awakening of the internal energetic currents.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This serves as a foundational bridge between physical Hatha yoga and the subtle body experiences of Rajayoga, emphasizing that posture is a tool for energetic regulation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Paścimatānāsana (Paschimottanasana), focused breathing, posture-based physiological manipulation.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is 'Prāṇa-sañcāra' within the 'Suṣumṇā-nāḍī', where 'paścimavahin' denotes the reversal of prāṇa's downward trend to an upward ascent.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern practice emphasizes spinal decompression and nervous system regulation; psychologically, this mirrors the 'grounding' effect of stretching to manage stress-induced physiological hyperarousal.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Asana (Mayurasana)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the physical configuration required for Mayurasana, or the Peacock Pose. It emphasizes the necessity of grounding and the precise alignment of the abdominal regions with the elbows to achieve balance.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: Mayurasana is a fundamental Hatha Yoga posture known for stimulating the digestive fire (jatharagni) and strengthening the abdominal core, mirroring the modern focus on functional anatomy and internal health.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practices are Hastanyasa (hand placement) and Nābhī-sthapana (navel stabilization), which are critical for maintaining balance and pressure for the Peacock Pose.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Jatharagni-uddipana, where the physical compression of the abdominal muscles by the kūrpara (elbows) serves to stimulate the internal digestive fire, central to the Hatha Yoga Pradipika.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern relevance lies in the psychosomatic regulation of digestion and the physical challenge of core stability, which helps in improving body awareness and reducing abdominal fat through deliberate sustained contraction.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Ayurvedic Hatha Yoga (Therapeutic Yoga)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse emphasizes the medicinal and therapeutic efficacy of specific yogic postures (asanas). It posits that physical discipline is not merely for spiritual elevation but acts as a curative agent for systemic biological malfunctions.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It highlights the integration of physical exercise and healthcare in ancient Indian traditions, bridging the gap between preventive wellness and remedial therapy.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Mayurasana (Peacock Pose) - the specific practice prescribed for stimulating gastric fire and removing internal toxins.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is 'Asana-prabhava' (the therapeutic potency of bodily alignment) specifically regarding the internal organs like Gulma (tumors/splenic issues) and Udara (abdominal disorders).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern physical therapy and bio-mechanics validate how core engagement and compression-decompression of abdominal viscera aid in digestive health, chronic inflammation, and visceral motility.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pratyahara and Kaya-sthairya (Stability of the body)
commentary_faqs.answer: Shavasana represents the highest state of physical surrender in yoga, where the practitioner simulates death to achieve complete muscular and mental relaxation. By consciously releasing tension, the individual transitions from egoic-driven activity to a state of profound stillness and non-attachment.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In the modern era of high-stress living and sedentary lifestyles, Shavasana serves as an essential psychological tool for 'de-stressing' and resetting the autonomic nervous system, bridging the gap between ancient asceticism and modern clinical relaxation techniques.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practice includes 'Supine posture', 'Complete relaxation' (śithilīkaraṇa), and 'Mindful stillness' (niścalatā).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Shavasana' (मृतकशयन) involves the neutralization of the 'Ahankara' through the simulation of the inert state of a 'Shava', leading to 'Citta-vritti-nirodha'.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: It acts as a primary tool for psychological grounding, anxiety reduction, and the management of psychosomatic fatigue, promoting deep nervous system regulation.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Explaining the superiority of the four asanas to be described hereafter, the text says 'caturaśīti'. Eighty-four asanas have been described by Shiva, the Lord. By the particle 'ca', it implies that there are eighty-four types or categories of asanas. As it is said by Gorakshanatha: 'The number of asanas is equal to the number of living species. Eighty-four types are cited for each.' Among those eighty-four described by Shiva, having selected the best ones, I will describe the four which are the essence, the best of all.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Parampara (Tradition) and Yogic Taxonomy
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse establishes the divine origin of Hatha Yoga practices, attributing the vast taxonomy of eighty-four postures to Lord Shiva. It emphasizes that yoga is a revealed knowledge (Agama) rather than a mere human invention, underscoring the diversity and depth of physical discipline available to the practitioner.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse serves as the foundation for the tradition of '84 Asanas,' which has become an iconic cultural marker of Indian heritage. In the modern context, it validates the complexity of physical yoga, bridging the gap between historical spiritual lore and the practice of maintaining bodily health.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribes the selection of 'Sārabhūta' (the essence) or the most excellent asanas from the wider pool, implying a hierarchical or functional approach to physical training.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is the 'Ishvara-prokta-yoga' (Yoga revealed by Shiva), categorizing 84,00,000 potential physical manifestations into 84 symbolic postures (caturaśīti-lakṣaṇāni), illustrating the diversity of Jiva-jāti (species).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, it acknowledges the somatic diversity of human existence, suggesting that there is a posture suited for every psychological or biological state, mirroring the modern shift towards personalized wellness and functional movement.

तदेव चतुष्कं नाम्ना निर्दिशति - सिद्धमिति । सिद्धं सिद्धासनम् । पद्मं पद्मासनम् । सिंहं सिंहासनम् । भद्रं भद्रासनम् इति चतुष्टयं श्रेष्ठम् अतिशयेन प्रशस्यम्, तत्रापि चतुष्टये सुखे सुखकरे सिद्धासने सदा तिष्ठेत् । एतेन सिद्धासनं चतुष्टयेऽप्युत्कृतमिति सूचितम् ॥ ३४ ॥

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These postures represent the bedrock of somatic self-regulation. In modern times, they serve as essential tools for stress reduction and maintaining structural integrity in a sedentary lifestyle.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The text prescribes 'sthana' (staying) in Siddhasana as the primary practice for practitioners seeking superior spiritual results.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Asana-Catushtaya' defines the foundational 'Sthira-sukha' principle, prioritizing Siddhasana as the 'Uttama' (superior) posture due to its utility in meditation.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, the selection of specific postures highlights the importance of 'postural ergonomics' to achieve a parasympathetic nervous system response, crucial for modern mindfulness and cognitive restoration.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
आसनचतुष्टयेऽप्युत्कृष्टत्वात् प्रथमं सिद्धासनमाह - योनिस्थानकमिति । योनिस्थानमेव योनिस्थानकम् । स्वार्थे कप्रत्ययः । गुदोपस्थयोर्मध्यमप्रदेशः योनिस्थानं तत् । अङ्घ्रिः वामश्चरणः तस्य मूलेन पार्ष्णिभागेन घटितं संलग्नं कृत्वा । स्थानान्तरम् एकं पादं दक्षिणं पादं मेढ्रेन्द्रियस्योपरिभागे दृढं यथा स्यात् तथा विन्यसेत् । हृदये हृदयसमीपे हनुं चिबुकं सुस्थिरं सम्यक् स्थिरं कृत्वा हनुहृदययोः चतुरङ्गुलमन्तरं यथा भवति तथा कृत्वा इति रहस्यम् । संयमितानि विषयेभ्यः परावृतानि इन्द्रियाणि येन स तथा । अचला या दृक् दृष्टिस्तया भ्रुवोरन्तरं मध्यं पश्येत् । हि प्रसिद्धं मोक्षस्य यत्कपाटं प्रतिबन्धकं तस्य भेदं नाशं जनयतीति तादृशम् । सिद्धानां योगिनाम् । आस्तेऽत्र , आस्यतेऽनेन इति वा आसनं सिद्धासनं नामक मिदं भवेदित्यर्थः ॥ ३५ ॥
मतान्तरे तु -

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Because Siddhasana is the most excellent among the four key postures, it is described first. 'Yoni-sthana' refers to the perineum, the region between the anus and the genitals. One should place the left heel against this area, and then place the other foot (the right one) firmly above the genital organ. By keeping the chin steady near the heart and fixing the gaze between the eyebrows, one attains the state that breaks the lock (kapata) of liberation. This is the posture of the Siddhas (the perfected ones).

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Posture (Asana)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the preliminary mechanics of Siddhasana, emphasizing the importance of applying physical pressure to the perineum to stabilize subtle energy (Prana). By physically blocking the downward flow of apana-vayu, the practitioner creates a base for meditative steadiness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: Siddhasana is historically considered the foremost of all postures for meditation. In modern times, it serves as a foundational technique for mindfulness and internal regulation, highlighting the interconnection between posture and mental composure.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practices are: 1. Proper placement of the heel against the perineum (Yoni-sthana), 2. Postural stability (dṛḍha-vinyāsa), 3. Jalandhara-bandha (chin lock/steadying the chin near the heart), and 4. Bhrumadhya-drishti (gazing between the eyebrows).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on 'Bandha' and 'Asana-siddhi'. The bhashya explains that the physical positioning (yonisthana) functions as a catalyst for internal energy modulation, facilitating the transition from bodily posture to spiritual emancipation (moksha-kapata-bheda).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this practice provides 'sensory withdrawal' (pratyahara). In a modern context, it acts as a psychosomatic technique to lower cortisol, stabilize the nervous system, and achieve a state of alert relaxation, which is conducive to sustained cognitive focus and stress management.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Having stated the Siddhasana accepted by Matsyendra, the author now speaks to state the variation accepted by others—'matāntare tu' (in the opinion of others). He demonstrates this: 'meḍhrāt' (from the genital). Placing the left ankle above the genitals, and likewise above that, not upon the left ankle, but above the primary foot—placing the other ankle, the right ankle, one should remain. This is the Siddhasana meant by other opinions.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Asana-vidhi (Posture Methodology)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse details the specific physical arrangement of the limbs required to achieve Siddhasana, a foundational meditative posture. By aligning the ankles specifically at the Mula-bandha region (genital area), the practitioner directs the flow of internal energy (Prana) to facilitate focused meditation.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This physical discipline remains a core component of Hatha Yoga and modern mindfulness practices, emphasizing the body-mind connection. It illustrates the yogic belief that somatic alignment directly influences psychological stability and spiritual awakening.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is Siddhāsana, emphasizing precise anatomical placement to stimulate the Mūlādhāra chakra area for meditation.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Siddhāsana as defined in different paramparas, focusing on the correct positioning of the gulpha (ankle) at the medhra (genital root) to achieve sthairya or stability in the nadi-samsthāna.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern relevance lies in postural ergonomics and neuro-physiological regulation; practitioners use these ancient techniques to reduce sympathetic nervous system arousal and cultivate deep meditative states.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: तत्र प्रथमं महासिद्धसम्मतमिति स्पष्टीकर्तुमस्यैव मतभेदान् नामभेदानाह - एतदिति । एतत् पूर्वोक्तं सिद्धासनं सिद्धासननामकं प्राहुः । केचिदित्यध्याहारः । अन्ये वज्रासनं वज्रासनसंज्ञकं विदुः जानन्ति । एके मुक्तासनं मुक्तासनाभिधं वदन्ति । परे गुप्तासनं गुप्तासनाख्यं प्राहुः । अत्रासनाभिज्ञाः । यत्र वामपादपार्ष्णिं योनिस्थाने नियोज्य दक्षिणपादपार्ष्णिः मेढ्रादुपरि स्थाप्यते तद्वज्रासनम् । यत्र तु दक्षिणसव्यपादपार्ष्णिद्वयमुपर्यधो भागेन संयोज्य योनिस्थानेन संयोज्यते तन्मुक्तासनम् । यत्र तु पूर्ववत् संयुक्तं पार्ष्णिद्वयं मेढ्रादुपरि निधीयते तद्गुप्तासनमिति ॥ ३७ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: In this context, to clarify that this is approved by the great Siddhas, the commentary addresses the variations in opinions and nomenclature. 'Etad' means the aforementioned Siddhasana. 'Some' is implied. 'Others' know it as Vajrasana. Some call it Muktasana, while others term it Guptasana. Regarding the definitions: that where the left heel is placed against the Yoni (perineum) and the right heel is placed above the penis is Vajrasana. Where the two heels are placed one above the other in contact with the perineum is Muktasana. Where the two heels joined as before are placed above the penis, that is Guptasana.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: यहाँ, यह स्पष्ट करने के लिए कि यह महासिद्धों द्वारा स्वीकृत है, भाष्यकार मतभेदों और नामभेदों को बताते हैं। 'एतत्' का अर्थ है पूर्वोक्त सिद्धासन। 'केचित्' (कुछ लोग) अध्याहार है। अन्य लोग इसे वज्रासन के नाम से जानते हैं। कुछ लोग इसे मुक्तासन कहते हैं। और अन्य इसे गुप्तासन कहते हैं। इन आसनों की परिभाषा यह है: जहाँ बायीं एड़ी को योनि-स्थान (पेरिनियल क्षेत्र) पर लगाकर दायीं एड़ी को मेढ्र (लिंग) के ऊपर स्थापित किया जाता है, वह वज्रासन है। जहाँ दोनों एड़ियों को एक-दूसरे के ऊपर संयोजित कर योनि-स्थान के पास रखा जाता है, वह मुक्तासन है। जहाँ एड़ियों को पूर्ववत जोड़कर मेढ्र के ऊपर रखा जाता है, वह गुप्तासन है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Yoga Asana Classification
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse highlights the traditional nomenclature variations within Hatha Yoga practice. It underscores that while names like Siddhasana, Vajrasana, Muktasana, and Guptasana differ, they often refer to nuanced variations in physical posture designed to regulate Prana.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This illustrates the diversity of pedagogical lineages in Indian tradition. It teaches practitioners not to be caught in semantic debates, but to focus on the technical precision and physiological impact of the posture on the subtle body (Nadis and Chakras).

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include precise placement of heels at the perineum and above the genital organs to stimulate the Mula-bandha and channel energy upwards.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around 'Asana-bheda' (postural variations) based on 'Siddha-sammatam' (the consensus of the accomplished). It emphasizes that technical precision regarding the placement of 'parshni' (heels) in relation to the 'yoni-sthana' and 'medhra' defines the subtle energy locks.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In a secular context, this highlights the necessity of expert instruction over generic labels. Psychologically, it emphasizes 'Sthira' (steadiness) and the alignment of the physical frame to facilitate meditative stillness, moving beyond the superficial view of asanas as mere exercise.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: अथ सप्तभिः श्लोकैः सिद्धासनं प्रशंसन्ति - यमेष्वित्यादिभिः । यमेषु मिताहारमिव । मिताहारो वक्ष्यमाणः ‘सुस्निग्धमधुराहारः’ (श्लो ५८) इत्यादिना । नियमेषु अहिंसामिव । सर्वाणि यान्यासनानि तेषु सिद्धाः एकं सिद्धासनं मुख्यं विदुरिति संबन्धः ॥ ३८ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Now, with seven verses, they praise the Siddhasana (the verse starting with 'Yameṣu'). Just as moderate diet is like the primary restraint among the Yamas (to be described later by the verse 'susnigdhamadhurāhāraḥ', verse 58), and non-violence is like the primary observance among the Niyamas. The connection is that among all postures, the perfected ones consider Siddhasana to be the supreme one.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: अब सात श्लोकों द्वारा सिद्धासन की प्रशंसा की जा रही है - 'यमेष्वित्यादिभिः'। यमों में मिताहार के समान। मिताहार जो आगे कहा जाएगा 'सुस्निग्धमधुराहारः' (श्लो ५८) इत्यादि के द्वारा। नियमों में अहिंसा के समान। जितने भी आसन हैं, उनमें सिद्धजन एक सिद्धासन को ही मुख्य मानते हैं, यही संबंध है ॥ ३८ ॥

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Primacy of foundational discipline in Yoga (Yama-Niyama)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse establishes a hierarchy within yogic ethics, suggesting that while all disciplines are necessary, certain virtues serve as the cornerstones of spiritual success. Mitahara (moderate diet) provides the physiological stability for Yamas, while Ahimsa (non-violence) provides the psychological foundation for Niyamas.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern life, this underscores the concept of 'essentialism' in health and ethics—prioritizing fundamental habits (like diet and empathy) as the basis for overall well-being and psychological resilience.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Mitahara (regulated diet) and Ahimsa (non-violence) as the central pillars for the practice of Siddhasana, essential for physical and mental equilibrium.
commentary_faqs.answer: The Bhashya emphasizes 'Siddhasana-prashamsa' (praise of Siddhasana) by drawing an analogy between the supremacy of specific yogic disciplines (Mitahara and Ahimsa) and the pre-eminence of Siddhasana as the supreme among asanas.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Reflects the psychological principle of prioritizing 'core habits'—regulating physical intake and interpersonal conduct to achieve a stable state of consciousness, comparable to the search for an optimal, balanced lifestyle in modern psychology.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: चतुरशीतीति । चतुरधिकाशीतिसङ्ख्याकानि यानि पीठानि तेषु सिद्धमेव सिद्धासनमेव सदा सर्वदाभ्यसेत् । सिद्धासनस्य सदाभ्यासे हेतुगर्भं विशेषणं द्वासप्ततिसहस्राणं नाडीनां मलशोधनं शोधकम् ॥ ३९ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Regarding the word 'caturaśīti': The eighty-four postures refer to the specific number of seats known in tradition. Among them, one must practice 'Siddham eva'—meaning 'Siddhasana alone'—at all times. The reasoning for this constant practice of Siddhasana is implied by its function: it acts as a purifier for the seventy-two thousand nadis (subtle energy channels) of the body.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Practice (Asana)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes the primacy of Siddhasana among the vast array of yoga postures. It asserts that for the purpose of spiritual refinement, the Siddhasana is the most essential and effective tool.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern yoga, this highlights the hierarchy of practices where foundational postures are prioritized over complex physical shapes for the sake of meditative stability and prana control.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Constant practice (Sada-abhyasa), Siddhasana (the perfected seat), and Nadi-shodhana (cleansing of the subtle channels).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Nadi-shodhana' through 'Siddhasana' serves as the primary technique for 'Chitta-shuddhi'. The commentary elucidates the 'Hetugarbha' (reason-contained) nature of the instruction, where the posture is not merely physical but a systemic energetic cleanser.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern mindfulness and somatic psychology emphasize the nervous system's regulation. Siddhasana serves as a 'bottom-up' approach to psychological stability by harmonizing the body's internal energy pathways to foster deep meditative concentration.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: आत्मध्यायीति । आत्मानं ध्यायतीत्यात्मध्यायी । मिताहारोऽस्यास्तीति मिताहरी । यावन्तो द्वादश वत्सराः यावद्-द्वादशवत्सरम् । ‘यावदवधारणे’ इत्यव्ययीभावः समासः । (पा.सू.२.१.८) । द्वादशवत्सरपर्यन्तमित्यर्थः । सदा सर्वदा सिद्धासनस्याभ्यासाद् योगी योगाभ्यासी निष्पत्तिं योगसिद्धिमाप्नुयात् प्राप्नुयात् । योगान्तराभ्यासमन्तरेण सिद्धासनाभयासमात्रेण सिद्धिं प्राप्नुयादित्यर्थः ॥ ४० ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Regarding 'Atmadhyayi': One who meditates on the Self is 'Atmadhyayi'. One who possesses measured diet is 'Mitahari'. 'Yavad-dvadasavatsaram' means for a duration of twelve years; this is an Avyayibhava compound according to the sutra (Pa.Su. 2.1.8) denoting 'up to that limit'. It implies the entire duration of twelve years. By constantly practicing 'Siddhasana', the Yogi attains perfection in Yoga. The intent is that even without other accessory yoga practices, one attains the goal merely through the practice of Siddhasana.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Yoga Siddhi through sustained discipline (Sadhana).
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse highlights the necessity of long-term commitment and physical regulation as prerequisites for deep meditative absorption. Self-meditation (Atmadhyana) acts as the internal focus, while dietary discipline (Mitahara) supports the biological stability required for sustained practice.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This emphasizes that spiritual or psychological mastery is not instantaneous but a product of 'Abhyasa' or persistent effort. In modern life, this underscores the '10,000-hour rule' equivalent in meditation, suggesting that neurological and psychological transformation requires time and consistency.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include Mitahara (moderation in food), Atmadhyana (internal meditation), and specifically the consistent, long-term practice of Siddhasana (the perfect posture).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on Atmadhyana (Self-contemplation) and the temporal limit of Sadhanakāla, emphasizing that consistent application over a specific duration (12 years) leads to the culmination of yoga (Niṣpatti).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: It suggests the psychological principle of 'neuroplasticity' where sustained, focused attention changes the brain structure, moving from conscious effort to innate mastery over time, applicable to any field requiring deep expertise or self-actualization.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Practice (Asana-siddhi)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes the primacy of Siddhasana over all other yogic postures, suggesting that mastery of one essential posture renders the variety of others redundant for the ultimate goal of yoga. It focuses on the economy of practice and the depth of stabilization.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern yoga culture, where physical variety is often prioritized, this verse acts as a reminder that the depth of meditative steadiness is far more important than the breadth of gymnastic ability.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Constant practice (abhyasa) of Siddhasana to attain steadiness (sthira) and concentration (ekagrata).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Asana-siddhi, where Siddhasana serves as the sarva-siddhikara or the foundational posture for Nadi-shodhana and Prana-nirodha, essential for the ascent of Kundalini.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: From a psychological perspective, this reflects the principle of 'focus over multitasking,' where deep mastery in a single discipline fosters greater mental clarity and emotional regulation than fragmented efforts across many.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Asana Siddhi (Perfection of Posture)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes the requirement of physical stability as a foundational prerequisite for higher meditative practices. By establishing the 'Siddhasana', the practitioner stabilizes the body to facilitate the stillness of the mind (citta-vritti-nirodha).

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This reflects the classical Hatha Yoga perspective that the body must be prepared as a steady vessel for the flow of Prana, relevant today for anyone practicing mindfulness and seeking physical poise in meditation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Siddhasana, Abhyasa (repeated practice), Sthirata (steadiness).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Asana-sthairya' represents the grounding of the physical form which is essential for 'Siddha-avastha', moving from gross anatomical stability to subtle energetic alignment.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this equates to creating a 'container' for deep cognitive work or neuro-modulation, where physical stillness (postural stability) acts as a signal to the autonomic nervous system to shift from the sympathetic to the parasympathetic state.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Excellence
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse emphasizes the supremacy of specific yogic techniques within the Hatha Yoga tradition. Siddhasana is hailed as the foundational posture for spiritual practice, while Kevala Kumbhaka is seen as the pinnacle of breath control leading to Samadhi.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These practices remain the bedrock of modern yoga training, emphasizing that physical and respiratory mastery are prerequisites for deep meditative states.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Regular practice of Siddhasana and the mastery of Kevala Kumbhaka as prescribed in Hatha Yoga Pradipika.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Kevala Kumbhaka' represents the 'kevala' or absolute state of suspension of breath, signifying the ultimate attainment beyond mere rhythmic regulation of prana.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: From a psychological perspective, these practices serve as techniques for nervous system regulation and mental stillness, crucial for managing contemporary stress and hyper-arousal.

commentary_faqs.answer: The verse serves as a transition to the instruction of physical discipline in Yoga. It highlights the importance of the physical vehicle (the body) as a foundation for meditative stability.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: Padmasana remains the quintessential symbol of meditative stillness in Indian culture, representing the balance between alertness and relaxation, widely used today for both spiritual practice and mental focus.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice of 'Asana' specifically targeting postural alignment and biological regulation.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is 'Asana' viewed as a foundational 'Sthira-sukha' (steadiness and comfort) necessary for 'Dhyana'.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents 'somatic regulation' where body posture influences the nervous system to achieve a state of 'relaxed alertness', essential for modern cognitive efficiency and stress reduction.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Guru-Parampara and Yogic Posture (Asana)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse establishes the authority of the Natha lineage in yogic practices. By citing Matsyendranatha, the text validates the efficacy and tradition of the Padmasana technique.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It emphasizes the importance of lineage (Parampara) in the transmission of knowledge, ensuring that physical disciplines are rooted in the wisdom of realized masters.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Padmasana; identification with the lineage of Matsyendranatha; systematic instruction of yogic postures.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Sampradaya-pramanya, wherein the physical practice of Asana derives its validity from the Guru's seal of approval (Abhimata).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this highlights the value of 'authoritative guidance' in maintaining discipline; it validates the importance of structure and tradition in a world of scattered wellness practices.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: नासाग्रे नासिकाग्रे विन्यसेद् विशेषेण निश्चलतया न्यसेदित्यर्थः । राजदन्तानां दंष्ट्राणां सव्यदक्षिणभागे स्थितानां मूले उभे मूलस्थाने जिह्वया उत्तम्भ्य ऊर्ध्वं स्तम्भयित्वा । गुरुमुखादवगन्तवयः अयं जिह्वाबन्धः । चिबुकं वक्षसि निधायेति शेषः । शनैः मन्दं मन्दं वायुमुत्थाप्य । अनेन मूलबन्धः प्रोक्तः । मूलबन्धोऽपि गुरुमुखादेव अवगन्तव्यः । वस्तुतस्तु जिह्वाबन्धेनैवायं चरितार्थ इति हठरहस्यविदः ॥ ४६ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary explains that 'Nāsāgre' means placing the tongue with great steadiness at the tip of the nose. 'Rājadantamūle' refers to the root of the teeth located on the left and right sides, where the tongue should be pressed or held upward. This technique, known as Jihvā-bandha, must be learned directly from a Guru. Along with fixing the chin upon the chest (Jalandhara Bandha) and gradually raising the Prana (breath), this process culminates in Mūlabandha. Ultimately, those learned in Hatha secrets maintain that the practice of Jihvā-bandha encompasses the essence of these locks.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Kechari Mudra / Jihva Bandha (Lingual Lock)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the physical positioning of the tongue to facilitate the internal circulation of Prana. By creating a lock (Bandha) with the tongue, the practitioner interrupts habitual mental fluctuations and redirects subtle energy inward.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern yoga, these techniques are recognized for their ability to induce states of autonomic nervous system balance and meditative focus, bridging the gap between physical asana and subtle pranic regulation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include Jihva Bandha (lingual lock), Jalandhara Bandha (chin lock), and the gradual raising of Vayu (breath/prana) under the direct supervision of a Guru.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around 'Jihva Bandha' and its integration with 'Mula Bandha', suggesting that the redirection of Prana (Pranotthapana) is the primary philosophical aim within the Hatha tradition.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this practice serves as a biofeedback mechanism. Modern practice emphasizes the stabilizing effect of such 'locks' on the vagus nerve and the stabilization of the mind during intense concentration exercises.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: In this manner, the posture in which one sits is called Padmasana; the term Padmasana is thus declared. The implied word is 'by those who know the postures'. What kind of posture is it? It is the destroyer of all diseases. It is rare for those lacking good fortune; however, it is attained and gained by the wise upon this earth.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga and Health
commentary_faqs.answer: Padmasana is regarded as a foundational yogic posture that aligns the body and balances the energy channels (Nadis). By stabilizing the physical form, it facilitates the cessation of physiological and psychosomatic ailments.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In the modern context, it serves as a primary tool for stress reduction, focus, and maintaining musculoskeletal health, bridging ancient physiological knowledge with current therapeutic practices.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Padmasana (Lotus Posture), Visesha-nashana (systematic eradication of ailments), and Dhira-labhyata (attainment through wisdom).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Sarvavyadhivinashana emphasizes the curative power of Asana through the balancing of Tridosha and energy stabilization within the Suksma-sharira.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, the stable posture encourages 'grounding,' while physiologically it aids metabolic regulation, acting as a preventative measure against chronic lifestyle disorders.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
एतच्च महायोगिसम्मतमिति स्पष्टयितुमन्यदपि पद्मासने कृत्यविशेषमाह - कृत्वेति । संपुटितौ संपुटीकृतौ करावुत्सङ्गस्थाविति शेषः । दृढतरम् अतिशयेन दृढं सुस्स्थं पद्मासनं बद्ध्वा कृत्वा इत्यर्थः । चिबुकं हनुं गाढं दृढं यथा स्यात् तथा वक्षसि वक्षः समीपे सन्निधाय सन्निहितं कृत्वा चतुरङ्गुलान्तरेणेति योगिसंप्रदायाज्ज्ञेयम् । जालन्धरबधं कृत्वा इत्यर्थः । तत् स्वस्वेष्टदेवतारूपं ब्रह्म वा । ‘ॐ तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणः त्रिविधः स्मृतः’ (भ.गी. १७.२३) इति भगवदुक्तेः , चेतसि चित्ते ध्यायन् चिन्तयन् । अपानमनिलम् अपानवायुं ऊर्ध्वं प्रोत्सारयन् मूलबन्धं कृत्वा सुषुम्नामार्गेण प्राणमूर्ध्वं नयन् पूरितं पूरकेण अन्तर्धारितं प्राणं न्यञ्चन् नीचैरधो अञ्चन् गमयन् । अन्तर्भावितण्यर्थोऽञ्चतिः । प्राणापानयोरैक्यं कृत्वेत्यर्थः । नरः पुमान् अतुलं बोधं निरुपमज्ञानं शक्तिप्रभावात् शक्तिः आधारशक्तिः कुण्डलिनी तस्याः प्रभावात् सामर्थ्यादुपैति प्राप्नोति । प्राणापानयोः ऐक्ये कुण्डलिनी भवति । कुण्डलिनी मार्गेण प्राणो ब्रहरन्ध्रं गच्छति । तत्र गते चित्तस्थैर्यं भवति ।
चित्तस्थैर्ये संयमाद् आत्मसाक्षात्कारो भवतीत्यर्थः ॥ ४८ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: To clarify that this is approved by the great Yogis, the commentator describes further actions in Padmasana. 'Samputitau' means the hands are joined and placed in the lap. 'Dridhataram' means making the posture very steady. Bringing the chin firmly to the chest constitutes the Jalandhara Bandha, with a gap of four fingers, as known from yogic tradition. By meditating in the heart on the Divine, and directing the Apana Vayu upwards while performing Mula Bandha, the practitioner unites Prana and Apana. Through the power of Kundalini, one attains incomparable knowledge (Atula Bodha). When Prana and Apana unite, Kundalini moves through the central channel to the Brahma-randhra, resulting in mental stability, which leads to the realization of the Self.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: यह महायोगियों द्वारा स्वीकृत है, यह स्पष्ट करने के लिए पद्मासन में अन्य कृत्यों को कहा गया है। संपुटितौ का अर्थ है- दोनों हाथों को आपस में जोड़कर उत्संग (गोद) में रखना। दृढतरम् का अर्थ है- आसन को बहुत स्थिर बनाना। हनु (ठुड्डी) को वक्षस्थल के समीप लाकर जालन्धर बन्ध करना, जिसे चार अंगुल के अंतराल के साथ योगी परंपरा से जानना चाहिए। चित्त में इष्टदेव का ध्यान करते हुए अपान वायु को ऊपर उठाकर मूलबन्ध करना और प्राण-अपान का ऐक्य करना। कुण्डलिनी शक्ति के प्रभाव से साधक अतुल बोध (ज्ञान) को प्राप्त करता है। प्राण और अपान के ऐक्य से कुण्डलिनी ब्रह्मरन्ध्र की ओर गमन करती है, जिससे चित्त की स्थिरता होती है और आत्मसाक्षात्कार होता है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Yoga-Asana and Pranayama integration
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse prescribes the foundational physical structure required for advanced meditation. By stabilizing the body and controlling the hands, the practitioner creates a vessel for internalizing energy and achieving mental stillness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These postures remain the cornerstone of Hatha Yoga globally, utilized today not only for spiritual growth but as recognized methods for stress reduction and autonomic nervous system regulation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Padmasana, Jalandhara Bandha, Mula Bandha, Prana-Apana unity.
commentary_faqs.answer: Sthirata of the body (asana) leading to the unification of Prana and Apana via Kundalini Shakti, culminating in Atmasakshatkara.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychophysiological regulation; the use of posture to achieve a 'flow state' and cognitive stillness in a high-distraction environment.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Physiology
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse describes the foundational physical state required for pranayama, emphasizing the alignment of the body (Padmasana) to facilitate the movement of prana through internal energy channels (nadis). It highlights that internal control of energy is dependent on the stable physical architecture of the body.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This is a quintessential instruction for modern practitioners, reminding us that mental and pranic stability is inextricably linked to physical discipline and posture in the tradition of Hatha Yoga.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Padmasana (Lotus Posture), Nadi-sanchara (Channel flow), and Prana-purana (Filling with vital energy).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept refers to Nadi-shodhana and the integration of Prana through the Suksma-sharira, utilizing the Padmasana as a Kshema (support) for internal purification.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern secular relevance includes postural ergonomics and nervous system regulation; psychologically, it addresses the 'grounding' effect of steady physical posture on the wandering mind.

commentary_faqs.answer: This verse introduces the formal 'Simhasana', which in yogic and ritual traditions represents the seat of authority, stability, and meditative steadiness. It signifies the transition from mundane actions to a focused, disciplined state of consciousness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It highlights the importance of physical and symbolic positioning in ancient Indian traditions, bridging the gap between external rituals and the internal stillness required for higher practice.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practice: Establishing a firm and auspicious base for meditation or authoritative action.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept focuses on Asana as a foundation for Sadhana, emphasizing the 'Simhasana' as a locus of authority and spiritual equilibrium (sthirata).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the creation of a 'sacred space' or a stable mindset necessary for productivity, focus, and mental executive function in a fast-paced environment.

commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the precise physical positioning required for specific yogic postures (asanas). The alignment of hands and fingers is not merely physical, but acts as a technique to stabilize the prana within the body during seated meditation or breathwork.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These instructions form the foundational somatic training in traditional Indian systems. Today, this represents the transition from simple stretching to the deliberate cultivation of 'sthira-sukham' (steadiness and ease) in the practice of mindful movement.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is 'Hastanyasa' (placing hands) and 'Anguli-prasarana' (extension of fingers) to establish postural alignment for internal balance.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is 'Asana-Sthiti' where physical anatomy is aligned to facilitate 'Pranayama' and concentration, ensuring the 'Sharira' becomes a stable vessel for meditative states.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern somatic therapy, such specific instructions reflect the principle of 'proprioceptive awareness,' helping individuals reduce cognitive load by engaging in repetitive, intentional physical grounding techniques.

commentary_faqs.answer: The verse establishes that physical discipline in Yoga is not merely mechanical but carries spiritual weight. The Simhasana is elevated to a sacred status through the endorsement of realized masters.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It emphasizes the importance of lineage and tradition in Yogic practice, where specific postures are validated by the spiritual authority of those who have mastered them.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is 'Simhasana' (The Lion Pose), categorized under Hatha Yoga techniques intended to stabilize the subtle energy channels.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Asana-Vidhi' relates to the authoritative validation of practices by yogic 'puṅgava' (great ones). It frames the posture as a sacred vessel for the practitioner's internal growth.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this reflects the 'placebo of authority' and the importance of intentionality—recognizing that the environment and the 'posture' we adopt significantly influence our mental state and focus.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
पार्श्वपादौ च पार्श्वसमीपगतौ पादौ पाणिभ्यां भुजाभ्यां दृढं बद्ध्वा परस्परसंलग्नाङ्गुलिभ्याम् उदरसंलग्नतलाभ्यां पाणिभ्यां बद्ध्वा इत्यर्थः ।
एतद् भद्रासनं भवेद् । कीदृशम् ? सर्वेषां व्याधीनां विशेषेण नाशनम् । गोरक्षेति । सिद्धाश्च ते योगिनश्च सिद्धयोगिनः, इदं भद्रासनं गोरक्षासनमित्याहुः । गोरक्षेण प्रायशः अभ्यस्तत्वाद् गोरक्षासनं वदन्ति ॥ ५४ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: ‘Pārśvapādau’ means the feet placed near the sides. ‘Pāṇibhyāṃ’ means with the arms, specifically grasping them firmly with fingers interlocked and palms touching the abdomen—this is the implied meaning. This becomes the Bhadrasana. What kind of asana is it? It is the destroyer of all diseases. Goraksha says: The Siddhas and Yogis—the Siddha-Yogis—call this Bhadrasana the Gorakshasana. Because it was frequently practiced by Goraksha, they call it Gorakshasana.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: पार्श्वपादौ का अर्थ है पार्श्व के समीप स्थित पाद। पाणिभ्यां का अर्थ है भुजाओं से, अर्थात परस्पर जुड़ी हुई उंगलियों से और उदर के साथ लगी हुई हथेलियों से उन्हें दृढ़तापूर्वक पकड़ना, यही इसका तात्पर्य है। यह भद्रासन है। यह कैसा है? यह सभी व्याधियों का विशेष रूप से नाश करने वाला है। गोरक्ष कहते हैं: सिद्ध और योगी—जिन्हें सिद्ध-योगी कहते हैं—इस भद्रासन को गोरक्षासन कहते हैं। चूंकि गोरक्ष द्वारा इसका प्रायः अभ्यास किया जाता था, इसलिए इसे गोरक्षासन कहते हैं।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Asana-Siddhi (Mastery of Posture)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the foundational physical mechanism for Bhadrasana. The practice emphasizes the synergy between the physical lock (Bandha) of the hands on the feet and the attainment of absolute physiological and mental stillness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern yoga, this highlights the transition from mere physical exercise to 'Sthira-Sukham' (steadiness and ease), which is the classic definition of asana in the Yoga Sutras.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is the ‘Bhadrasana’ or ‘Gorakshasana’, characterized by firm grasping of the feet and achieving absolute physical immobility to induce internal balance.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on ‘Sthiratā’ (steadiness) achieved through the ‘Bandha’ (lock) of the body, transforming a physical posture into a ‘Rogashamana’ (disease-destroying) therapeutic tool as cited by Goraksha.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this asana serves as a somatic intervention for anxiety and restlessness; by achieving physical immobility, one creates a feedback loop that leads to the stabilization of the nervous system and mental focus.

commentary_faqs.answer: The verse describes the state where the physical body no longer acts as a source of limitation or exhaustion for the practitioner. By perfecting the posture (āsana-bandha), the yogi attains a state of stillness that transcends physical fatigue.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In the modern era, this serves as a reminder that the goal of yoga is not just physical exercise but the stabilization of the mind. By mastering the body, one achieves the mental endurance required for deep meditative states.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practice includes the perfection of postural discipline (āsana-bandha) to eliminate bodily exhaustion (vigata-śrama).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Sthira-Sukham Asanam, where the yogi achieves transcendence over physical limitations through specific āsana-bandha.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this refers to achieving a 'flow state' where the individual operates without the interference of physiological stress or cognitive fatigue.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Sadhana
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse categorizes the essential components of Hatha Yoga practice: physical stability through postures, vitality through breath control, and energy manipulation through mudras. These practices act as a preparatory framework to refine the physical vehicle for deeper spiritual inquiry.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These classical techniques provide a structured methodology for psychosomatic health, emphasizing the regulation of the life-force (Prana) to achieve mental stability in an increasingly distracted modern society.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include: Asana (posture), Kumbhaka (breath retention), and Mudra (gesture/energy seal), leading to the final stage of Nada-anusandhana.
commentary_faqs.answer: The bhashya highlights the concept of 'Hathasiddhi' and 'Anusandhana' of the 'Anahata' sound as the ultimate objective of the preparatory yogic limbs.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents a transition from gross physiological regulation to subtle mental monitoring, analogous to modern mindfulness techniques that rely on biofeedback and breath control to stabilize the nervous system.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Yogic Discipline (Sadhana-Chatushtaya)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse outlines the foundational qualifications required for success in yogic practices. It emphasizes the balance between physical discipline, dietary control, and internal mental focus.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These virtues act as a psychological framework to minimize external distractions, allowing the practitioner to channel energy efficiently toward self-realization in both classical and contemporary contexts.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Brahmacharya (continence), Mitahara (moderate diet), Tyaga (renunciation/non-attachment), and Yoga-parayana (total dedication).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Sadhana-shuddhi, where physical, moral, and intentional discipline acts as a catalyst for Siddhi (attainment).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: This serves as a manual for metabolic health and cognitive focus; 'Mitahara' aligns with modern nutritional science, while 'Brahmacharya' and 'Tyaga' reflect the psychological benefits of minimizing dopamine-driven distractions.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
पूर्वश्लोके मिताहारीत्युक्तं, तत्र योगिनां कीदृशो मिताहारः इत्यपेक्षायामाह -
‘द्वौ भागौ पूरयेदन्नैः तोयेनैकं प्रपूरयेत् ।
शिवो जीवः ईश्वरः वा । ‘भोक्ता देवो महेश्वरः’ इति वचनत् । तस्य संप्रीत्यै सम्यक् प्रीत्यर्थं यो भुञ्जते स मिताहार इत्युच्यते ॥ ५८ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Regarding the previous verse mentioning 'Mitahara' (measured diet), an expectation arises regarding the nature of this diet for a Yogi. The text explains: 'Fill two parts with food, one part with water, and leave the fourth part empty.' This is for the satisfaction of Shiva, Jiva, or Ishvara, as it is said, 'The consumer is the divine Lord Maheshvara.' One who eats with this intention is called a Mitahari (one of measured diet).

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: पूर्व श्लोक में 'मिताहारी' के उल्लेख के उपरांत यह जिज्ञासा होती है कि योगियों का मिताहार कैसा होना चाहिए। इस पर कहा गया है: 'दो भाग अन्न से, एक भाग जल से पूर्ण करना चाहिए, और चतुर्थ भाग को रिक्त रखना चाहिए।' यह शिव, जीव अथवा ईश्वर की संतुष्टि के लिए है, क्योंकि कहा गया है 'भोक्ता देवो महेश्वरः' (खाने वाला स्वयं महेश्वर है)। जो व्यक्ति इसी भावना से भोजन करता है, वही मिताहारी कहलाता है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Mitahara (Measured Diet)
commentary_faqs.answer: Mitahara is the yogic discipline of diet, emphasizing not just what we eat but how we eat. It balances the physical body's need for sustenance with the spiritual need for lightness, ensuring the digestive process does not interfere with meditative focus.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This serves as a cornerstone for modern mindful eating and dietary ethics, promoting health through portion control and the selection of sattvic (pure) ingredients.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice involves portion control (Chaturthansha-vivarjita) and the mental attitude of dedication (Samprityartham).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept focuses on Bhoktri-bhava (the attitude of the consumer), where eating is transformed into a Yajna (offering) to the Divine within, rather than mere sense gratification.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this shifts the focus from calories to consciousness, providing a structured approach to prevent overeating and promote digestive harmony.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: अथ योगिनामपथ्यमाह द्वाभ्याम् - कट्विति । कटु कारवेल्ल इत्यादि, अम्लं चिञ्चाफलादि, तीक्ष्णं मरीचादि, लवणं प्रसिद्धं, उष्णं गुडादि, हरीतशाकं पत्रशाकं, सौवीरं काञ्जिकं, तैलं तिलसर्षपादिस्नेहः, तिलाः प्रसिद्धाः, सर्षपाः सिद्धार्थाः, मद्यं सुरा, मत्स्यो झषः । एषामितरेतरद्वन्द्वः । एतानपथ्यानाहुः । अजस्येदम् आजं तदादिः यस्य सौकरादेः तदाजादि तच्च तन्मांसं च आजादिमांसम्, दधि दुग्धपरिणामविशेषः, तक्रं गृहीतसारं दधि, कुलत्थो द्विदलविशेषः, कोलं कोल्याः फलं बदरम् । ‘कर्कन्धूर्बदरी कोलिः’ इत्यमरः (२.४.३६) । पिण्याकं तिलपिण्डं, हिङ्गु रामठं, लशुनम् । एषामितरेतरद्वन्द्वः । एतानि आद्यानि यस्य तत्तथा । आद्यशब्देन पलाण्डुगृञ्जनमादकद्रव्यमाषान्नादिकं ग्राह्यम् । अपथ्यम् अहितम् । योगिनामिति शेषः । आहुः योगिनः इत्यध्याहारः ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Now, the author discusses the non-beneficial (apathya) items for yogis in two verses, beginning with 'kaṭu'. 'Kaṭu' refers to bitter gourd (karavella), etc.; 'amla' to tamarind fruit, etc.; 'tīkṣṇa' to black pepper, etc.; 'lavaṇa' is well-known; 'uṣṇa' refers to jaggery, etc.; 'hārītaśāka' refers to leafy greens. Sauviraka is fermented rice water (kanjika); taila is oil from sesame, mustard, etc.; tila is well-known; sarṣapa refers to white mustard; madya is alcohol; matsya is fish. There is a mutual dual (itaretara-dvandva) compound of these. These are called apathya (unwholesome). 'Āja' refers to that which belongs to a goat, and 'ājdādi' refers to the meat of such animals like pigs, etc. Dadhi is a specific modification of milk; takra is buttermilk with butter removed; kulattha is a specific type of pulse (horse gram); kola is the fruit of the jujube (badara). 'Karkandhūrbadarī koliḥ' is stated in the Amarakosha (2.4.36). Piṇyāka is sesame cake, hiṅgu is asafoetida, laśuna is garlic. These are in a mutual dual compound. These items, starting from these, are meant by the word 'ādya'. Through the word 'ādya', one should include onions (palāṇḍu), shallots (gṛñjana), intoxicating substances, black gram (māṣa), and grains. 'Apathyam' means unwholesome. The word 'yoginām' (for yogis) is implied. 'Āhuḥ' (they say) means the yogis say—this is supplied contextually.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: अब योगी के लिए अपथ्य का वर्णन दो श्लोकों में करते हैं - 'कटु' इत्यादि से। कटु यानी करेला आदि, अम्ल यानी इमली आदि, तीक्ष्ण यानी मिर्च आदि, लवण यानी नमक, उष्ण यानी गुड़ आदि, हरीतशाक यानी पत्रशाक। सौवीर का अर्थ है कांजी, तैल यानी तिल-सरसों का स्नेह, तिल प्रसिद्ध है, सर्षप यानी सिद्धार्थ (सफेद सरसों), मद्य यानी सुरा, मत्स्य यानी मछली। इन सबका इतरेतर द्वंद्व है। इन्हें अपथ्य कहा गया है। अज से संबंधित 'आज', आदि का अर्थ है सूकर आदि, उसका मांस 'आजादिमांस'। दधि दूध का परिणाम है, तक्र यानी मथा हुआ दही, कुलत्थ एक प्रकार की दाल है, कोल यानी बेर का फल। 'कर्कन्धूर्बदरी कोलिः' यह अमरकोष में कहा गया है। पिण्याक यानी तिल की खली, हिङ्गु यानी हींग, लशुन यानी लहसुन। इनका इतरेतर द्वंद्व है। इन पदार्थों से आरम्भ होने वाले (आद्य) पदार्थ यहाँ ग्राह्य हैं। आद्य शब्द से पलाण्डु (प्याज), गृञ्जन, मादक द्रव्य और माष (उड़द) आदि ग्रहण करने चाहिए। अपथ्य का अर्थ है अहितकर। योगियों के लिए, यह शेष (अध्याहार) है। 'आहुः' यानी योगियों का कथन है, ऐसा अध्याहार करना चाहिए।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Ahara-vijnana (Science of Dietetics for Yogis)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse serves as the introduction to the list of prohibited foods (apathya) for a practitioner of Yoga. It emphasizes that physical health and physiological balance are foundational requirements for higher spiritual states.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern life, this correlates to the 'gut-brain axis,' where dietary discipline is viewed as essential for emotional regulation, mental clarity, and the maintenance of a calm nervous system.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is Ahara-niyama (dietary regulation) and the avoidance of substances that induce stimulation or dullness, specifically focusing on Sattvic diet to maintain internal equilibrium.
commentary_faqs.answer: The bhashya highlights the concept of Ahara-vijnana where diet is classified into Pathya (wholesome) and Apathya (unwholesome) based on their Raga-Dvesha inducing properties and Guna influence (Rajas/Tamas).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern relevance lies in mindfulness of consumption (dietary hygiene), recognizing how specific chemical compositions of food impact the CNS and psychosomatic health, a precursor to mental focus in any cognitive or meditative task.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
’अथ वर्ज्यानि वक्ष्यामि योगविघ्नकराणि च ।
लवणं सर्षपं चाम्लमुग्रं तीक्ष्णं च रूक्षकम् ।
स्कन्दपुराणेऽपि - ‘त्यजेत् कट्वम्ललवणं क्षीरभोजी सदा भवेत्’ इति । अम्लयुक्तम्् अम्लद्रव्येण युक्तमपि त्याज्यं किमुत साक्षादम्लम् । अत्र तृतीयपादं ‘पललं वा तिलपिण्डम्’ इति केचित् पठन्ति । तस्यायमर्थः । पललं मांसं , तिलपिण्डं पिण्याकं कदशनं कदन्नं यावनालकोद्रवादि, शाकं विहितेतरशाकमात्रम्, उत्कटं विदाहि, मिरचीति लोके प्रसिद्धं, मिरचा इति हिन्दुस्थानभाषायाम् । कदशनादीनां समाहारद्वन्द्वः । अतिलवणादिकं वर्ज्यं वर्जनार्हम् । दुष्टमिति पाठे दुष्टं पूतिपर्युषितादि । अहितमिति योजनीयम् ॥ ६० ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Now I shall state the forbidden items that cause obstacles to Yoga: salt, mustard, sour, pungent, sharp, and dry things. The Skanda Purana also says, 'One should avoid pungent, sour, and salty items; one should always be a consumer of milk.' Even food mixed with sour substances should be abandoned, let alone direct sourness. Some read the third foot as 'palalam va tilapindam' (meat or sesame-cake). Its meaning is: Palala means meat; Tilapinda means sesame oil-cake; Kadasana means poor quality grains like millet or kodo; Shaka means restricted vegetables; Utkata means burning/inflammatory (such as chili, famous in the world as 'mirchi'). All such items, along with excessive salt, are to be avoided. If the reading is 'dushtam' (corrupt), it refers to putrid or stale food; this should also be understood as unwholesome.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: अब मैं योग में विघ्न डालने वाले वर्ज्य पदार्थों को कहता हूँ: लवण, सरसों, अम्ल, उग्र, तीक्ष्ण और रूक्ष पदार्थों का त्याग करना चाहिए। स्कन्द पुराण में भी कहा गया है कि कटु, अम्ल और लवण का त्याग कर सदैव क्षीरभोगी होना चाहिए। अम्लद्रव्य से युक्त भोजन भी त्याज्य है, सीधे अम्ल की तो बात ही क्या। कुछ लोग तृतीय पाद में 'पललं वा तिलपिण्डम्' पाठ पढ़ते हैं। इसका अर्थ है: पलल यानी मांस, तिलपिण्ड यानी पिण्याक (खली), कदशन यानी निकृष्ट अन्न (जैसे कोदव आदि), शाक यानी निषिद्ध शाक, उत्कट यानी दाहक (जो लोक में मिरची नाम से प्रसिद्ध है)। इन सबका समाहार वर्जनीय है। दुष्ट शब्द होने पर इसका अर्थ पूति या पर्युषित (बासी) भोजन है, जिसे अहितकर ही मानना चाहिए।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Ahara-Shuddhi (Purity of Diet for Yoga)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes that for a practitioner, the quality of food is not just about nutrition but about its energetic effect on the body and mind. Reheated and dry foods are considered 'tamasic' or 'rajasic', creating impurities that obstruct the subtle channels (nadis) required for higher states of meditation.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this aligns with the preference for 'freshly prepared' (sattvic) food over processed or microwave-reheated leftovers. It highlights the importance of vitality (prana) in food, suggesting that psychological clarity is inextricably linked to physiological freshness.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Mitahara (measured diet), avoidance of Tamasic foods, preference for freshly cooked sattvic meals, and restraint from inflammatory stimulants.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept focuses on Ahara-Vihara regulation, specifically identifying Ahita (unwholesome) substances that create Dosha imbalances, hindering Dhyana-siddhi.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Provides a framework for mindful eating; addresses the physiological burden of processed food and chronic inflammation caused by refined ingredients in contemporary diets.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Having stated the things to be avoided by yogis always, the author now speaks of what to avoid during the practice (Abhyasa) in this half-verse. 'Vahni' (Fire/Heat), 'Stri' (Women/Carnal company), and 'Pantha' (Roads/Travel). Their service—meaning, excessive proximity to fire, excessive sexual association, and unnecessary travel—should be avoided at the beginning of one's practice. However, once the practice is established, these may be done occasionally. The use of 'Adi' (etc.) implies that for a householder, sitting by a fire in winter, visiting one's wife during the proper season, or travel for pilgrimage is not prohibited, and the author cites Goraksha's authority for this.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: योगियों के लिए सदा वर्ज्य वस्तुओं को बताने के बाद, अब अभ्यास-काल में वर्जनीय वस्तुओं को आधे श्लोक द्वारा कहा जा रहा है। 'वह्नि', 'स्त्री', और 'पन्था'—इनका सेवन, अर्थात् अग्नि के पास बैठना, स्त्री-संसर्ग, और तीर्थ-यात्रा आदि, अभ्यास के प्रारंभ में इनका वर्जन (त्याग) करना चाहिए। अभ्यास सिद्ध होने पर कदाचित ये निषिद्ध नहीं हैं। 'आदि' शब्द से यह सूचित होता है कि गृहस्थ के लिए शीतकाल में अग्नि-सेवन, ऋतुकाल में स्वपत्नी-गमन और तीर्थ-यात्रा के लिए मार्ग-गमन निषिद्ध नहीं है। यहाँ प्रमाण के रूप में गोरक्ष-वचन को उद्धृत किया गया है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Yogic Restraint (Yama/Niyama context)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse emphasizes the necessity of conserving Prana and minimizing external distractions (Vikshesas) during the initial stages of Sadhana. By limiting exposure to heat (Vahni), sensory indulgence (Stri), and physical exhaustion through travel (Pathi), the practitioner creates a stable environment for internal focus.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In the modern context, this serves as a guideline for managing sensory input and avoiding burnout in an hyper-stimulated world, emphasizing that spiritual progress requires a period of simplified, disciplined living.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prarambhika-Sadhana (Initial practice), Indriya-Nigraha (Sense restraint), and situational moderation as permitted by the Bhashyakara for householders.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Vairagya and Prana-Samrakshana (preservation of vital energy) is central, identifying these as 'Vighnakara' (obstacles) in the initial stage of Kundalini or Hatha Yoga practice.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this translates to 'digital and environmental detox'. It underscores the need for a 'focused space' to cultivate deep, sustained attention (Ekagrata) before engaging with the complexities of the world.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
अथ योगिपथ्यमाह - गोधूमेत्यादिना । गोधूमाश्च शालयश्च यवाश्च षाष्टिकाश्च षष्ट्या दिनैः ये पच्यन्ते तण्डुलविशेषाः ते, शोभनमन्नं पवित्रान्नं श्यामाकनीवारादि तच्च एतेषां समाहारद्वन्द्वः । शुण्ठी प्रसिद्धा, पटोलकफलं परवर इति भाषायां प्रसिद्धं शाकं तदादिः यस्य कोशातक्यादेः तत्पटोलकफलादिकं ‘शेषाद्विभाषा’ (पा.सू. ५.४.१५४) इति कप्रत्ययः । पञ्चानां शाकानां समाहारः पञ्चशाकम् । तदुक्तं वैद्यके -
‘सर्वशाकमचाक्षुष्यं चाक्षुष्यं शाकपञ्चकम् ।
मुद्गा द्विदलविशेषा आदिः यस्य तन्मुद्गादि । अदिपदेन आढकी ग्राह्या । दिव्यं निर्दोषमुदकं जलम् । यम एषामस्तीति यमिनः तेष्विन्द्रो देवश्रेष्ठो यो योगीन्द्रः तस्य पथ्यं हितम् ॥ ६२ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Now, the author speaks of diet suitable for a Yogi, beginning with 'Godhuma...'. Wheat, Sali (rice), Yava (barley), and Shastika (a specific rice variety maturing in sixty days) constitute the grains. 'Sobhanannam' refers to pure food like Shyama and Nivara. These form a Samahara-dvandva compound. The text also mentions Patola (pointed gourd) and Mudga (green gram) and other pulses as beneficial. Such food is described as 'Pathya' (wholesome) for a Yogi, the foremost among those who practice self-control.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pathya-Ahara (Dietetic Prescription for Yogis)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse emphasizes the importance of 'Sattvic' and easily digestible grains in the yogic diet. By prescribing specific grains, the text highlights that physical and mental stability (Yogasiddhi) are grounded in the quality of nourishment consumed.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It serves as a foundational guideline for metabolic health and mental clarity, reinforcing the traditional wisdom that 'you are what you eat', which is highly relevant in modern nutritional psychiatry.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Selection of specific 'dhanya' (grains like Shali, Yava) and 'shaka' (vegetables like Patola) to maintain 'dhatu-samya' (equilibrium of bodily constituents).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept centers on 'Pathyahara' (wholesome diet) as a prerequisite for 'Yogic Siddhi', strictly classifying food based on 'Sattva' guna and 'Pavitrata' (purity).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Relates to the modern understanding of 'gut-brain axis' where specific fiber-rich and easily digestible foods are correlated with reduced inflammation and improved cognitive function.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Ahara-Vidhi (Dietary Principles)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the ideal characteristics of food for a practitioner (yogi), emphasizing quality and compatibility with physiological health. It highlights the importance of satvika ahara in maintaining the internal balance of bodily dhatus.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It serves as a foundational guideline for Ayurvedic nutrition, asserting that quality food is essential for physical health and mental stability in daily living.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Mitahara (measured diet), consumption of Sattvika substances, prioritizing fresh dairy derivatives (Gavya) for internal lubrication.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Dhatupraposhana' refers to the systemic nourishment of the seven bodily tissues (dhatus) essential for maintaining prana and physical vitality during the practice of yoga.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychological nutrition recognizes that the quality of nutrients directly impacts emotional stability and stress regulation, mirroring the verse's emphasis on food as a substrate for mental and physical endurance.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Sarva-adhikaratva (Universality of Yoga)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse asserts that the path of Yoga is not restricted by biological or physical conditions such as age or infirmity. It emphasizes the inclusive nature of Yogic practice, suggesting that the spirit of Yoga transcends bodily limitations.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this dispels the common myth that Yoga is only for the fit, young, or flexible, making it a powerful therapeutic and inclusive tool for the aging population and those with health challenges.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Constant practice (abhyasa) regardless of physical status; adapting the practice to individual capacity.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Sarva-adhikaratva, implying that Yoga as a spiritual science is open to every jiva regardless of Deha-avastha (bodily condition).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this promotes accessibility and inclusivity, counteracting body-shaming and promoting mental resilience through modified practice for all physical demographics.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Importance of Consistent Practice (Abhyasa-Yoga)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse asserts that spiritual or material success is fundamentally dependent on 'kriya' or dedicated action. Without the application of effort, the desired outcome remains unattainable, emphasizing that theoretical knowledge without practice is sterile.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This mirrors the modern scientific and psychological understanding of 'deliberate practice' where mastery in any field (sports, arts, or spiritual development) is the result of persistent engagement rather than innate potential alone.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice prescribed is 'Kriya' (systematic execution) and 'Abhyasa' (constant, repetitive effort), which are the essential requirements for reaching a state of perfection.
commentary_faqs.answer: The bhashya highlights 'Abhyasa' as the indispensable cause of 'Siddhi', asserting that 'kriya' is the necessary bridge between intent and attainment.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In a secular context, this highlights the necessity of 'execution' in business and self-development, suggesting that procrastination or mere contemplation leads to stagnation, whereas iterative action drives progress.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Authenticity and Inner Practice
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes that spiritual perfection (Siddhi) is not an external achievement or a result of superficial appearance. It advocates for an internal transformation rather than performative displays of spirituality.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In a world dominated by image and branding, this serves as a reminder that true growth is intrinsic. It warns against the 'theatre of spirituality' that often prioritizes appearance over actual discipline.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Avoidance of performative spirituality and emphasis on internal Sadhana or direct meditative absorption.
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse critiques externalism, stating that Siddhi (spiritual accomplishment) is not a product of 'Vesha' (costume) or 'Katha' (theoretical discourse), but a result of internal Tattva-jnana.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: This reflects the modern psychological need for 'authenticity' over 'image-management' on social media, advocating for genuine skill and internal development over public signaling of success.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: योगाङ्गनुष्ठानस्य अवधिमाह - पीठानीति । पीठान्यासनानि चित्रा अनेकविधाः कुम्भकाः सूर्यभेदादयः दिव्यन्युत्कृष्टानि करणानि महामुद्रादीनि, हठसिद्धौ प्रकृष्टोपकारकत्वं करणत्वम् । हठाभ्यासे सर्वाणि पीठकुम्भककरणानि राजयोगफलावधि राजयोगः एव फलं तदवधि तत्पर्यन्तं कर्तव्यानि इति शेषः ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The text states the duration/limit of practicing the limbs of yoga: 'pīṭhāni' means the postures (asanas). 'Citrāḥ kumbhakāḥ' refers to various types like Sūryabhedana. 'Divyāni karaṇāni' refers to excellent techniques like Mahāmudrā; they are called 'karaṇa' because they are highly instrumental in achieving perfection in Hatha Yoga. In Hatha practice, all these postures, breath retentions, and techniques should be performed until the fruit of Raja Yoga is attained.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: योगाङ्ग अनुष्ठान की अवधि बताते हुए कहा गया है - पीठ अर्थात आसन, विविध प्रकार के कुम्भक जैसे सूर्यभेदन आदि, तथा दिव्य अर्थात उत्कृष्ट करण (महामुद्रा आदि)। हठसिद्धि में जो प्रकृष्ट उपकारक हैं, उन्हें 'करण' कहा जाता है। हठाभ्यास में इन सभी पीठ, कुम्भक और करणों का तब तक अभ्यास करना चाहिए जब तक राजयोग रूपी फल की प्राप्ति न हो जाए।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Hatha Yoga Practice (Sadhana)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse highlights the foundational tools of Hatha Yoga: physical postures, breath control, and advanced energetic locks. These are not ends in themselves but functional instruments (karaṇa) meant to stabilize the body and mind for higher states of consciousness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These practices remain relevant in modern yoga as the fundamental physical framework for developing somatic health and mental regulation, bridging the gap between physiological fitness and meditative stillness.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include: 1. Pīṭhāni (Asanas), 2. Citra-kumbhaka (varieties of breath retention like Sūryabhedana), and 3. Divya-karaṇa (internal locks and energy seals like Mahāmudrā).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Karaṇa' defines internal physiological and energetic tools (like Mahāmudrā) that serve as catalysts for 'Hatha-siddhi' (attainment in Hatha Yoga), specifically aiming for the ultimate 'Rāja-yoga' state.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern relevance lies in the intentionality of movement; the verse emphasizes that physical and respiratory exercises should have a psychophysical objective (Rāja-yoga) rather than remaining purely athletic or aesthetic.
